sections.name: Health Care Careers, Professionalism, Learning, and Problem-Solving

items.q: What is the first step in the problem-solving process?
items.ex: You can't solve a problem until you clearly know what it is, so identifying it comes first.
w: set goals
Goals and solutions come after you know what the real problem is.
Gather information
Gathering information is a later step; first define the problem.
Evaluate the results
Evaluating results is the last step, after a solution is tried.
tf: The first step in the problem-solving process is to identify the problem.
The first step in the problem-solving process is to set goals.
Goals and solutions follow; the process starts by identifying the problem.

alt.q: When working through a problem, which step should come before all the others?
alt.ex: You must know exactly what the problem is before you can solve it.
w: Gather information
Information gathering follows once the problem is defined.
Choose the best solution
Choosing a solution comes later in the process.
Evaluate the results
Evaluating results is the final step.

alt.q: A pharmacy technician notices that prescriptions are often filled late. Using the problem-solving process, what should the technician do first?
alt.a: Figure out exactly what the real problem is
alt.ex: Problem solving always begins by identifying the real problem.
w: Pick a new workflow and start using it
Choosing and acting on a solution comes after the problem is identified.
Collect coworkers' ideas for possible fixes
Gathering ideas comes after the problem is clearly defined.
Check whether a change reduced the delays
Checking results is the last step, not the first.

items.q: Working well with other people is necessary only in health care jobs that involve working directly with patients.
items.ex: Teamwork matters in every health care job, including non-patient roles like billing or IT.
items.ww: Teamwork is needed in all health care jobs, not just direct patient care roles.

alt.q: Only health care workers who provide hands-on patient care need to be able to work well with others.
alt.ex: Every health care job, including non-patient roles, requires working well with others.
alt.ww: Teamwork is not limited to direct patient care roles.

alt.q: Health care workers in non-patient roles, such as billing or medical records, also need to work well with others.
alt.ex: Teamwork is needed in all health care jobs, not just patient care roles.
alt.ww: Non-patient roles still depend on cooperation with coworkers and other departments.

items.q: Which of the following refers to being placed on an official list after meeting educational and testing requirements?
items.ex: Registration means being placed on an official list (registry) after meeting education and testing requirements.
w: Licensure
Licensure is legal permission from a state to practice an occupation.
Certification
Certification is recognition, often by a professional organization, that you met its standards.
Accreditation
Accreditation applies to schools, programs, or facilities that meet set standards, not individuals.
tf: Registration means being placed on an official list after meeting educational and testing requirements.
Accreditation means placing an individual on an official list after meeting educational and testing requirements.
Accreditation recognizes schools, programs, or facilities, not individual workers.

alt.q: What term describes having your name added to an official list once you have met required education and testing standards?
alt.ex: Registration means being placed on an official list after meeting education and testing requirements.
w: Licensure
Licensure is legal permission from a state to practice an occupation.
Certification
Certification is recognition that a person has met an organization's standards.
Accreditation
Accreditation applies to schools, programs, or facilities, not individuals.

alt.q: A health care worker finishes the required education, passes an exam, and is then placed on an official registry. What is this process called?
alt.ex: Being placed on an official list after education and testing is registration.
w: Accreditation
Accreditation is for programs and facilities, not individual workers.
Licensure
Licensure is state legal permission to practice, not placement on a list.
Certification
Certification is recognition of meeting standards, not being listed on a registry.

items.q: Which of the following statements would be considered an opinion?
items.a: "People who don't have jobs and lack medical insurance are just too lazy to work."
items.ex: An opinion is a personal judgment that can't be proven; calling people "lazy" is a belief, not a fact.
w: "Medicare is a federal health insurance program for people 65 and older."
This can be verified, so it is a fact.
"The patient's temperature was recorded at 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit."
A measured, recorded value is a fact.
"Some people without jobs do not have employer-sponsored health insurance."
This is a verifiable fact, not a judgment.
ms: Which of the following statements are opinions? (Select all that apply)
"People who don't have jobs and lack medical insurance are just too lazy to work."
A judgment about people that can't be proven.
"Nurses are the most caring people in health care."
"Most caring" is a personal judgment, not measurable fact.
"The patient's temperature was recorded at 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit."
A recorded measurement is a fact.
"Medicare is a federal health insurance program for people 65 and older."
This can be verified, so it is a fact.
"The clinic is open Monday through Friday."
Office hours can be checked, so this is a fact.

alt.q: Which statement expresses a personal belief rather than a fact that can be proven?
alt.a: "People who don't have jobs and lack medical insurance are just too lazy to work."
alt.ex: Calling people lazy is a personal judgment that cannot be proven, so it is an opinion.
w: "Medicare is a federal health insurance program for people 65 and older."
This can be verified, so it is a fact.
"The patient's blood pressure reading was 120/80."
A measured, recorded value is a fact.
"The clinic opens at 8:00 a.m. on weekdays."
Business hours can be checked, so this is a fact.

alt.q: A coworker says, "Patients without insurance are just too lazy to work." How is this statement best described?
alt.a: An opinion, because it is a personal judgment that cannot be proven
alt.ex: The statement is a belief about people, not something that can be verified.
w: A fact, because it describes a group of people
Describing a group does not make a judgment provable.
A fact, because some uninsured people are unemployed
Being unemployed does not prove anyone is lazy.
An objective observation, because it was stated clearly
Objective information is observed or measured, not a personal judgment.

items.q: Which of the following is the best example of the meaning of integrity?
items.a: A person strives to always tell the truth.
items.ex: Integrity means being honest and acting on strong moral principles, such as always telling the truth.
w: A person always arrives at work on time.
Punctuality shows dependability rather than honesty.
A person follows the dress code every day.
Following the dress code reflects professional appearance.
A person learns new skills to advance their career.
Learning new skills reflects lifelong learning and ambition.

alt.q: Which behavior best shows that a person has integrity?
alt.ex: Integrity means being honest and acting on strong moral principles.
w: Always arriving at work on time
Punctuality shows dependability rather than honesty.
Keeping a neat, professional appearance
Appearance reflects grooming, not honesty.
Taking classes to advance a career
Taking classes reflects ambition and learning, not honesty.

alt.q: A medical assistant gives a patient the wrong handout by mistake and immediately tells the supervisor the truth about it. Which quality does this best show?
alt.ex: Being honest about a mistake shows integrity.
w: Punctuality
Punctuality means being on time.
Manual dexterity
Manual dexterity is skill in using the hands.
Professional appearance
Professional appearance refers to dress and grooming.

items.q: There are many ways you can start to practice the qualities of health care professionals while you are in school.
items.ex: Students can practice professional qualities now, such as being on time, prepared, honest, and respectful.
items.ww: School offers many chances to build professional habits before entering the workforce.

alt.q: Students can begin building the qualities expected of health care professionals before they finish school.
alt.ex: Habits like being on time, prepared, honest, and respectful can be practiced in school.
alt.ww: School offers many chances to practice professional qualities now.

alt.q: Professional qualities can only be developed after a person is hired into a health care job.
alt.ex: Students can practice professional qualities while they are still in school.
alt.ww: School provides many chances to build professional habits before employment.

items.q: Which of the following levels typically requires the most education?
items.ex: Professional-level positions (e.g., physicians, pharmacists) typically require a bachelor's degree or higher.
w: Technologist
Technologists usually need less education than professionals, often an associate or bachelor's.
Aide
Aides are entry level with short training, the least education.
Assistant
Assistants typically need a certificate or associate degree, less than professionals.

alt.q: Of these occupational levels, which usually calls for the greatest amount of education?
alt.ex: Professional-level positions typically require a bachelor's degree or higher.
w: Technologist
Technologists usually need less education than professionals.
Aide
Aides are entry level with the least training.
Assistant
Assistants usually need a certificate or associate degree.

alt.q: A student wants a health care career at the level that requires the most schooling, such as physician or pharmacist. Which level should they plan for?
alt.ex: Physicians and pharmacists are professional-level jobs requiring the most education.
w: Aide level
Aide positions are entry level with short training.
Assistant level
Assistant positions require much less education than professionals.
Technologist level
Technologists generally need less education than professionals.

items.q: The best way to prepare for a test is to _____.
items.a: spend some time studying every day
items.ex: Studying a little every day builds understanding and retention better than cramming.
w: study all night before the exam
Cramming causes fatigue and poor long-term retention.
reread the textbook the morning of the test
Last-minute rereading doesn't build real understanding.
memorize only the instructor's lecture notes
Lectures can't cover everything; you need broader study.
tf: Spending some time studying every day is the best way to prepare for a test.
Studying all night before the exam is the best way to prepare for a test.
Cramming leads to fatigue and poor retention; daily study works better.

alt.q: Which study habit is the most effective way to get ready for an exam?
alt.a: Studying for some time each day
alt.ex: Regular daily study builds understanding and retention better than cramming.
w: Staying up all night studying before the exam
Cramming causes fatigue and poor retention.
Rereading the textbook the morning of the exam
Last-minute rereading does not build real understanding.
Memorizing only the instructor's lecture notes
Lectures cannot cover everything you need to know.

alt.q: A phlebotomy student has a final exam in three weeks. Which study plan is best?
alt.a: Review the material for a while every day until the exam
alt.ex: Spending some time studying every day is the best way to prepare.
w: Wait until the night before and study all night
Cramming leads to fatigue and poor long-term retention.
Skim the textbook the morning of the exam
Last-minute skimming does not build understanding.
Study only the instructor's lecture slides
Lectures cover only part of what students need to learn.

items.q: A student has received poor grades in their Math for Medical Assistants class. If they use the five-step problem-solving process, what should be their first step?
items.ex: The five-step process always begins by identifying the real problem, such as why the grades are low.
w: Gather information about tutoring options
Gathering information comes after the real problem is identified.
Choose the best possible solution
Choosing a solution comes later in the process.
Drop the class and retake it later
Acting before identifying the problem skips the process.

alt.q: A student's grades in a medical math course are low. According to the five-step problem-solving method, how should the student begin?
alt.a: Determine what the real problem is
alt.ex: The five-step process always starts by identifying the real problem.
w: Look up tutoring services
Gathering information comes after the problem is identified.
Pick the best solution and act on it
Choosing a solution comes later in the process.
Check whether the solution improved the grades
Evaluating results is the last step.

alt.q: A nursing assistant student keeps failing skills checkoffs and decides to use the five-step problem-solving process. Which action comes first?
alt.a: Figure out the real reason the checkoffs are being failed
alt.ex: Identifying the real problem is always the first step.
w: Ask classmates which practice methods work for them
Gathering information comes after the problem is identified.
Sign up for extra lab practice sessions
Choosing a solution comes later in the process.
Review whether extra practice improved results
Evaluating results is the final step.

items.q: Which of the following might be helpful to returning adult students who are trying to manage multiple responsibilities?
items.a: Start each day with a list of what needs to be accomplished
items.ex: A daily to-do list helps adult learners prioritize and manage school, work, and family duties.
w: Study only when there is free time left over
Busy adults rarely have leftover time; studying needs to be scheduled.
Handle tasks as they come up without planning
Without planning, important tasks get missed or delayed.
Put off assignments until the night before
Procrastination adds stress and lowers quality.
ms: Which strategies help returning adult students manage multiple responsibilities? (Select all that apply)
Start each day with a list of what needs to be accomplished
A daily list helps prioritize competing tasks.
Set goals and prioritize tasks
Goals and priorities guide where time is spent.
Put off assignments until the night before
Procrastination adds stress and lowers quality.
Handle tasks as they come up without planning
Without planning, important tasks get missed.
Cut back on sleep to fit everything in
Sleep loss hurts learning and health.

alt.q: An adult returning to school is juggling work, family, and classes. Which strategy would help most?
alt.a: Making a list each morning of tasks to complete that day
alt.ex: A daily to-do list helps adult learners prioritize many responsibilities.
w: Studying only when free time happens to be left over
Busy adults rarely have leftover time, so study must be scheduled.
Handling tasks as they come up without planning
Without planning, important tasks get missed.
Putting off assignments until the night before
Procrastination adds stress and lowers quality.

alt.q: Maria works part-time, cares for her parents, and attends a medical coding program. Which habit would best help her manage her responsibilities?
alt.a: Starting each day by listing what she needs to get done
alt.ex: A daily list helps her prioritize school, work, and family duties.
w: Doing tasks only as they come up
Reacting without a plan causes important tasks to be missed.
Saving assignments until the night before they are due
Procrastination increases stress and lowers quality.
Studying only if she has extra free time
With many duties, extra free time rarely appears.

items.q: What is the name for a provider who specializes in treating the kidneys?
items.ex: Nephr/o means kidney, so a nephrologist specializes in treating the kidneys.
w: Orthopedist
An orthopedist treats bones, joints, and muscles.
Neurologist
A neurologist treats the brain and nervous system.
Oncologist
An oncologist treats cancer.
tf: A nephrologist is a provider who specializes in treating the kidneys.
A neurologist is a provider who specializes in treating the kidneys.
Neurologists treat the nervous system; nephr/o means kidney.
ms: Which provider-specialty pairs are correctly matched? (Select all that apply)
Nephrologist - kidneys
Nephr/o means kidney.
Neurologist - nervous system
Neur/o means nerve.
Oncologist - kidneys
Oncologists treat cancer, not the kidneys specifically.
Orthopedist - heart
Orthopedists treat bones and joints; cardiologists treat the heart.

alt.q: A physician whose specialty is disorders of the kidneys is called a(n):
alt.ex: Nephr/o means kidney, so a nephrologist treats the kidneys.
w: Neurologist
A neurologist treats the brain and nervous system.
Gastroenterologist
A gastroenterologist treats the digestive system.
Dermatologist
A dermatologist treats the skin.

alt.q: A patient's lab results show declining kidney function. Which specialist would the primary care provider most likely refer them to?
alt.ex: Nephrologists specialize in treating the kidneys.
w: Cardiologist
A cardiologist treats the heart.
Pulmonologist
A pulmonologist treats the lungs.
Oncologist
An oncologist treats cancer.

items.q: Which of the following occupations would likely require the highest degree of manual dexterity?
items.ex: Dental hygienists use fine hand instruments in the small space of the mouth, demanding high manual dexterity.
w: Coding specialist
Coding is mainly computer and record work, not fine hand skills.
Pharmacy technician
Counting and measuring medications needs some dexterity, but less precise instrument work.
Occupational therapy assistant
OTAs guide patients through activities; precise instrument work is less central.

alt.q: Which of these health care jobs depends most on precise, skilled hand movements?
alt.ex: Dental hygienists use fine instruments in the small space of the mouth.
w: Coding specialist
Coding is mainly computer and record work.
Medical receptionist
Reception work centers on scheduling and communication, not fine instrument work.
Health services manager
Managers focus on planning and administration, not hands-on procedures.

alt.q: A student has excellent fine motor control and enjoys detailed work with small hand instruments. Which occupation best uses this strength?
alt.ex: Dental hygiene requires a high degree of manual dexterity with small instruments.
w: Coding specialist
Coding relies on knowledge of codes and records, not fine hand skills.
Health services manager
Management work is administrative rather than hands-on.
Medical receptionist
Receptionists mainly schedule, greet, and communicate with patients.

items.q: Each occupational area has positions that require different amounts of education and training and involve varying amounts of responsibility. Collectively, what are these levels known as?
items.ex: Career ladders are the levels within an occupational area, each with more education and responsibility.
w: Career clusters
Career clusters group related occupations, not levels within one occupation.
Scopes of practice
Scope of practice is what a worker is legally allowed to do.
Job descriptions
A job description lists duties of one position, not the levels.
tf: The levels of positions within an occupational area are collectively known as career ladders.
The levels of positions within an occupational area are collectively known as career clusters.
Career clusters group related occupations; levels within one area are career ladders.

alt.q: What term describes the set of levels within an occupational area, each requiring different education and carrying different responsibility?
alt.ex: Career ladders are the levels within an occupation, rising in education and responsibility.
w: Career clusters
Career clusters group related occupations, not levels within one.
Scopes of practice
Scope of practice is what a worker is legally allowed to do.
Job descriptions
A job description lists the duties of one position.

alt.q: In nursing, positions range from nursing assistant to licensed practical nurse to registered nurse, each with more education and responsibility. Together, these levels form a:
alt.ex: Levels in one occupational area with increasing education and responsibility make a career ladder.
w: Career cluster
A career cluster is a grouping of related occupations.
Scope of practice
Scope of practice defines legally allowed duties for one role.
Professional organization
A professional organization is a group that members of a profession join.

items.q: The Occupational Outlook Handbook contains a list of accredited schools for various health care occupations.
items.ex: The Occupational Outlook Handbook describes duties, education, pay, and job outlook, not accredited schools.
items.ww: It provides career information, not a list of accredited schools.

alt.q: Accredited schools for health care occupations are listed in the Occupational Outlook Handbook.
alt.ex: The Handbook gives career information, not a list of accredited schools.
alt.ww: It describes duties, education, pay, and outlook rather than listing schools.

alt.q: The Occupational Outlook Handbook gives information such as job duties, required education, pay, and job outlook.
alt.ex: The Handbook is a source of career information like duties, education, pay, and outlook.
alt.ww: Providing this career information is exactly what the Handbook does.

items.q: Which of the following is not considered subjective data?
items.ex: Signs are objective: observed or measured by the provider, so they are not subjective data.
w: symptoms
Symptoms are what the patient reports, so they are subjective.
Patient's description of pain
Pain as the patient describes it is subjective.
chief complaint
The chief complaint is stated in the patient's own words, so it is subjective.
tf: Signs are objective data that the provider observes or measures.
Signs are subjective data reported by the patient.
Patient-reported data are symptoms; signs are observed or measured.
ms: Which of the following are objective data? (Select all that apply)
Blood pressure reading
Measured by the provider, so objective.
Rash seen on inspection
An observed sign, so objective.
Patient says they feel dizzy
Reported by the patient, so subjective.
Patient's chief complaint
Stated in the patient's own words, so subjective.
Patient's pain rating of 7/10
Self-reported, so subjective.

alt.q: Which type of patient information is objective rather than subjective?
alt.ex: Signs are observed or measured by the health care professional, so they are objective.
w: Symptoms
Symptoms are reported by the patient, so they are subjective.
Chief complaint
The chief complaint is given in the patient's own words.
Patient's description of pain
Pain as described by the patient is subjective.

alt.q: A medical assistant records several items during a visit. Which one is NOT subjective data?
alt.a: A blood pressure of 140/90 measured by the assistant
alt.ex: A measured value is a sign, which is objective data.
w: The patient says they feel dizzy
This is reported by the patient, so it is subjective.
The patient reports nausea since yesterday
This is a patient-reported symptom, so it is subjective.
The patient states the visit is for a headache
A chief complaint in the patient's words is subjective.

items.q: Which of the following is an advantage that many adult students have over younger students?
items.a: They have life experiences they can apply to their studies.
items.ex: Adult students can connect new material to work and life experiences, which aids learning.
w: They usually have fewer outside responsibilities.
Adult students often juggle jobs and families, so they have more.
They have more free time for studying.
Work and family duties usually leave adults less free time.
They have more recent experience taking tests.
Younger students are usually more recently in school.
tf: Many adult students can apply their life experiences to their studies.
Adult students generally have fewer outside responsibilities than younger students.
Adults often balance work and family, so they usually have more responsibilities.

alt.q: Compared with younger students, what benefit do many adult learners bring to their studies?
alt.a: Life experience they can connect to what they are learning
alt.ex: Adults can relate new material to their work and life experience.
w: Fewer responsibilities outside of school
Adult students often have jobs and families, so they have more.
More free time for studying
Work and family duties usually leave adults less free time.
More recent experience taking tests
Younger students have usually been in school more recently.

alt.q: Dana, age 42, worked in a daycare center before entering a pediatric medical assistant program. What advantage does she likely have?
alt.a: She can apply her past experience with children to her coursework
alt.ex: Adult students can use life experiences to support their learning.
w: She has fewer responsibilities outside school
Adult students usually have more outside responsibilities, not fewer.
She has more free time to study
Adults often have less free time because of work and family.
She has taken tests more recently than her classmates
Younger classmates have usually been in school more recently.

items.q: Good instructors should include everything students need to know for their future careers in their lectures.
items.ex: No instructor can cover everything; students must also read, research, and keep learning on their own.
items.ww: Lectures can't include everything a career requires; self-directed study is also needed.

alt.q: A good instructor's lectures should cover everything a student will need to know for their future career.
alt.ex: No lecture can cover everything; students must also learn on their own.
alt.ww: Careers require more knowledge than any set of lectures can include.

alt.q: Students should expect to learn some career knowledge on their own, beyond what instructors cover in lectures.
alt.ex: Lectures cannot include everything, so self-directed study is also needed.
alt.ww: Relying only on lectures leaves gaps in career knowledge.

items.q: When choosing a career, which of the following considerations is most likely to lead to career success?
items.ex: Matching a career to your personality and natural abilities makes you more likely to enjoy it and succeed.
w: The salary the job pays
Pay alone doesn't ensure you'll be suited to or succeed in the work.
The jobs your friends have chosen
Friends' choices don't reflect your own strengths and interests.
The occupations with the most job openings
Openings matter, but fit with your abilities drives success.

alt.q: What should most guide a career choice if the goal is long-term success in that career?
alt.a: How well the career fits your personality and natural abilities
alt.ex: A good fit with your personality and abilities makes success more likely.
w: How much the job pays
Pay alone does not mean you are suited to the work.
Which careers your friends have chosen
Friends' choices do not reflect your own strengths.
Which occupations have the most openings
Openings matter, but personal fit drives success.

alt.q: Leo is detail-oriented, enjoys computers, and prefers limited patient contact. Which approach to choosing a health career will most likely lead to his success?
alt.a: Choose a career that fits his personality and abilities
alt.ex: Matching a career to personality and natural abilities is most likely to bring success.
w: Choose the career with the highest starting pay
High pay does not guarantee a good fit or success.
Choose the same career as his best friend
A friend's choice may not match Leo's strengths.
Choose whichever career has the most local openings
Job availability alone ignores whether he is suited to the work.

items.q: On the job, you should use thinking and problem-solving skills _____.
items.ex: Health care workers face decisions constantly, so critical thinking is needed at all times.
w: only when a supervisor asks
Thinking skills are part of every task, not just on request.
only during emergencies
Routine tasks also require judgment to keep patients safe.
only when patients are present
Non-patient tasks like records and supplies also need good judgment.
tf: Health care workers should use thinking and problem-solving skills at all times on the job.
Health care workers need thinking and problem-solving skills only during emergencies.
Routine tasks also require judgment, so these skills are used at all times.

alt.q: When should a health care worker apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills on the job?
alt.ex: Health care work involves constant decisions, so thinking skills are always needed.
w: Only when a supervisor asks
Thinking skills are part of every task, not just on request.
Only during emergencies
Routine tasks also require judgment to keep patients safe.
Only when patients are present
Non-patient tasks also require good judgment.

alt.q: A sterile processing technician mostly works away from patients, cleaning and packaging surgical instruments. When does this worker need to use thinking skills?
alt.ex: Thinking and problem-solving skills should be used at all times on the job.
w: Only when patients are nearby
Non-patient tasks like instrument processing still require judgment.
Only when the supervisor gives an instruction
Good judgment is part of every task, not just directed ones.
Only during an emergency
Routine work also needs careful thinking to keep patients safe.

items.q: A student has just started a dental assisting program. They want to do well in school, but they need to find reliable daycare for their two young children. They decide to use the five-step problem-solving process. What would they do as the last step in the process?
items.a: Evaluate how the chosen solution has worked out
items.ex: The final step is evaluating whether the chosen solution worked and adjusting if it did not.
w: Identify the real problem
Identifying the problem is the first step, not the last.
Gather information about daycare options
Gathering information is an early step.
Choose the best daycare option
Choosing a solution comes before evaluating how it worked.
tf: The last step of the five-step problem-solving process is to evaluate how the chosen solution has worked out.
The last step of the five-step problem-solving process is to choose the best solution.
After choosing and trying a solution, you still must evaluate the results.

alt.q: In the five-step problem-solving process, what is the final step?
alt.a: Evaluate how well the chosen solution worked
alt.ex: The last step is checking whether the solution worked and adjusting if needed.
w: Identify the real problem
Identifying the problem is the first step.
Gather information about possible options
Gathering information is an early step.
Choose the best solution
Choosing a solution comes before evaluating it.

alt.q: A medical office changed its appointment reminder system to reduce no-shows. Following the five-step problem-solving process, what should the staff do last?
alt.a: Check whether the new reminder system actually reduced no-shows
alt.ex: The final step is evaluating how the chosen solution has worked out.
w: Identify why patients are missing appointments
Identifying the problem is the first step.
Gather information about different reminder systems
Gathering information happens early in the process.
Select the reminder system that seems best
Selecting a solution comes before evaluating it.

items.q: Students must acquire more information in their classes than what is needed to pass tests in their classes.
items.ex: Classes build knowledge for the job, so students should learn beyond what is needed to pass tests.
items.ww: Tests sample only part of what you need; careers require deeper, broader knowledge.

alt.q: Students should aim to learn more in class than just what they need to pass the tests.
alt.ex: Classes build job knowledge, which goes beyond what tests measure.
alt.ww: Tests sample only part of what a career requires.

alt.q: Learning only the material needed to pass class tests is enough to prepare a student for a health care career.
alt.ex: Careers require deeper, broader knowledge than tests alone measure.
alt.ww: Students must learn more than what is needed to pass tests.

items.q: A surgical technologist is preparing a patient for surgery. The patient seems extremely nervous and is crying. As a thinking health care professional, what should the surgical technologist do?
items.a: Use questions to determine why the patient is nervous and upset
items.ex: A thinking professional asks questions to find the cause of the patient's distress before responding.
w: Tell the patient that everything will be fine
False reassurance dismisses concerns without learning what is wrong.
Continue the preparations without comment
Ignoring visible distress misses important information and is uncaring.
Leave and ask another staff member to take over
Leaving avoids the problem instead of addressing the patient's needs.

alt.q: A patient about to have surgery is crying and appears very anxious. What is the best response from a surgical technologist who thinks critically?
alt.a: Ask questions to find out why the patient is upset
alt.ex: Asking questions finds the cause of the distress before deciding how to respond.
w: Tell the patient that everything will be fine
False reassurance dismisses concerns without learning the cause.
Continue preparing the patient without comment
Ignoring visible distress misses important information.
Leave and ask another staff member to take over
Leaving avoids the patient's needs instead of addressing them.

alt.q: A patient waiting for an X-ray is shaking and in tears. What should the radiologic technologist do?

items.a: Ray works in the computer department at a large hospital. The hospital recently had a water leak, and Ray was asked to assist in moving some supplies to a dry location. He readily agreed to assist.
items.ex: Ray readily helped outside his usual duties, showing flexibility and teamwork, which are professional behaviors.
w: Susan has worked in a medical office for one year. She feels that the tasks she performs have become routine, and she takes things for granted.
Taking tasks for granted shows poor attention to technical skills.
Matt complains to his patients about his coworkers.
Complaining to patients about coworkers is unprofessional.
Lisa, a medical assistant, refused to help a coworker restock supplies because it was not in her job description.
Refusing to help teammates shows poor teamwork.

alt.q: Which health care worker is showing professional behavior?
alt.a: Ray, who works in a hospital's computer department, readily agrees to help move supplies away from a water leak when asked.
alt.ex: Ray willingly helps outside his usual duties, showing flexibility and teamwork.
w: Susan has worked in a medical office for a year and now takes her routine tasks for granted.
Taking tasks for granted shows poor attention to technical skills.
Matt complains to his patients about his coworkers.
Complaining to patients about coworkers is unprofessional.
Lisa refuses to help a coworker restock supplies because it is not in her job description.
Refusing to help teammates shows poor teamwork.

alt.q: During a busy flu clinic, a medical records clerk is asked to help hand out forms and direct patients. Which response is most professional?
alt.a: Readily agree to help where needed
alt.ex: Willingly helping outside usual duties shows teamwork and professional behavior.
w: Refuse because the task is not in the job description
Refusing to help shows poor teamwork.
Complain to patients about being short-staffed
Complaining to patients is unprofessional.
Agree, but do the task carelessly because it is routine
Taking tasks for granted is not professional.

items.q: Oral and written communication, interpersonal relations, basic computer skills, and time management are important skills for success in health care. The BEST term to describe these skills is _____.
items.ex: Communication, interpersonal, computer, and time management skills are non-technical skills used in every health job.
w: technical skills
Technical skills are job-specific procedures like taking vital signs.
clinical skills
Clinical skills are hands-on patient care tasks.
expanded scope of practice
Expanded scope of practice means cross-training to become multiskilled.
tf: Oral and written communication, interpersonal relations, computer skills, and time management are non-technical skills.
Oral and written communication, interpersonal relations, computer skills, and time management are technical skills.
Technical skills are job-specific procedures; these general skills are non-technical.
ms: Which of the following are non-technical skills? (Select all that apply)
Time management
A general work skill used in every job.
Oral and written communication
Communication is a non-technical skill.
Interpersonal relations
Getting along with others is non-technical.
Giving an intramuscular injection
A job-specific clinical procedure, so technical.
Taking a blood pressure reading
A job-specific clinical procedure, so technical.

alt.q: Skills such as communication, interpersonal relations, basic computer use, and time management, needed for success in health care, are best called:
alt.ex: These skills apply across all health care jobs and are non-technical skills.
w: Technical skills
Technical skills are job-specific procedures like taking vital signs.
Clinical skills
Clinical skills are hands-on patient care tasks.
Expanded scope of practice
Expanded scope of practice means cross-training to become multiskilled.

alt.q: A hiring manager is impressed that a job candidate writes clear emails, gets along well with others, uses basic computer programs, and manages time well. These are examples of:
alt.ex: Communication, interpersonal, computer, and time management skills are non-technical skills.
w: Technical skills
Technical skills are specific procedures of a particular job.
Clinical skills
Clinical skills involve hands-on patient care.
Expanded scope of practice
Expanded scope of practice refers to cross-training in multiple skills.

items.q: The ability to encourage people to work together to achieve common goals, inspire others, and promote positive change is called _____.
items.ex: Leadership is inspiring others, encouraging teamwork toward common goals, and promoting positive change.
w: professionalism
Professionalism is overall professional conduct, the trait leaders should model.
mentoring
Mentoring is an experienced person guiding a less-experienced one.
supervision
Supervision is overseeing and directing others' work.
tf: Leadership is the ability to encourage people to work together toward common goals and promote positive change.
Supervision is the ability to inspire others, encourage teamwork toward common goals, and promote positive change.
Supervision means overseeing work; inspiring teamwork and change is leadership.

alt.q: What quality involves inspiring others, getting people to cooperate toward shared goals, and promoting positive change?
alt.ex: Leadership is inspiring others and encouraging teamwork toward common goals and positive change.
w: Mentoring
Mentoring is an experienced person guiding a less-experienced one.
Attitude
Attitude is the positive or negative way a person thinks or feels.
Professional distancing
Professional distancing is caring for patients without a personal relationship.

alt.q: A respiratory therapist motivates her team to work together to reduce patient wait times and encourages new ideas for improvement. Which quality is she showing?
alt.ex: Inspiring a team toward a common goal and positive change is leadership.
w: Mentoring
Mentoring is one-on-one guidance of a less-experienced worker.
Professional distancing
Professional distancing concerns boundaries with patients.
Self-directed learning
Self-directed learning is managing your own education.

items.q: Robert has been a health care professional for twenty years. He began his career when he graduated from a technical school program. He has completed in-service education offerings from his employer, continuing education offerings from his professional organization, and other formal and informal education. Robert has participated in which of the following? Choose the BEST answer.
items.ex: Ongoing education across a whole career, formal and informal, is lifelong learning.
w: continuing medical education
CE courses are only one part of Robert's learning, not the whole picture.
career ladder
A career ladder is levels of jobs and responsibility, not ongoing education.
in-service training
In-service is employer-provided training, only one piece of what Robert did.

alt.q: Which term BEST describes continuing to gain knowledge through formal and informal education across an entire health care career?
alt.ex: Ongoing education throughout a whole career, formal and informal, is lifelong learning.
w: Continuing education credits
CE credits are only one part of career-long learning.
Career ladder
A career ladder is levels of jobs, not ongoing education.
In-service training
In-service is employer training, only one piece of career-long learning.

alt.q: A medical assistant who graduated 15 years ago still attends workplace trainings, takes online CE courses, and reads health journals at home. What is she practicing?
alt.ex: She keeps learning in many ways throughout her career, which is lifelong learning.
w: In-service training
Workplace training is only one of the ways she is learning.
Career ladder
A career ladder is moving up job levels, not ongoing education.
Specialization
Specialization narrows job focus; it does not describe ongoing education.

items.q: Meeting established professionals, supporting legislation on behalf of your profession, and earning continuing education credits are all advantages of _____.
items.ex: Professional organizations offer networking, advocacy for the profession, and continuing education credits.
w: obtaining a state license
A license grants legal permission to practice; it does not provide networking or advocacy.
climbing the career ladder
Moving up a career ladder means advancing levels, not organizational membership benefits.
completing an associate degree
A degree is entry education; it does not involve legislation or networking.
tf: Professional organizations offer continuing education and advocate for legislation on behalf of their profession.
Professional organizations grant the state license required to practice a health care occupation.
Licenses are granted by state agencies and boards, not professional organizations.
ms: Which of the following are advantages of joining a professional organization? (Select all that apply)
Meeting established professionals in your field
Networking with experienced members is a key benefit.
Supporting legislation on behalf of your profession
Organizations advocate for laws affecting their profession.
Earning continuing education credits
Many organizations offer CE courses and credits.
Automatically receiving a state license
Licensure comes from the state, not from membership.
Guaranteed job placement after graduation
Membership helps networking but does not guarantee a job.

alt.q: Networking with experienced professionals, advocating for laws that affect your profession, and earning CE credits are benefits of which of the following?
alt.ex: Professional organizations offer networking, legislative advocacy, and continuing education credits.
w: Obtaining a state license
A license grants legal permission to practice, not networking or advocacy.
Climbing the career ladder
Advancing job levels does not provide organizational membership benefits.
Completing an associate degree
A degree is entry education; it does not involve advocacy or networking.

alt.q: A new dental hygienist wants to meet experienced colleagues, help support laws affecting her field, and earn CE credits. What would BEST meet all three goals?
alt.a: Joining a professional organization for dental hygienists
alt.ex: Professional organizations provide networking, advocacy for the profession, and CE credits.
w: Renewing her state license
Licensure allows practice but offers no networking or advocacy.
Asking for a promotion at work
A promotion changes her job level, not these professional benefits.
Taking a single college course
One course gives knowledge, not networking or advocacy.

items.q: Which of the following statements is NOT an example of professional communication in the health care setting?
items.ex: No one can know exactly how another feels; the phrase can sound dismissive of the patient.
w: "Can you tell me more about what is worrying you?"
Open-ended questions invite the patient to share; this is professional.
"I'm not sure, but I will find out and let you know."
Being honest and following up is professional communication.
"It sounds like you are worried about the procedure."
Reflecting feelings shows listening without claiming to share them.
tf: Telling a patient "I know exactly how you feel" is not considered professional communication.
Telling a patient "I know exactly how you feel" is a good way to show empathy.
You cannot truly know another's feelings, so the phrase can seem dismissive.

alt.q: Which statement to a patient would be considered UNPROFESSIONAL communication?
alt.ex: No one can truly know another's feelings; the phrase can seem dismissive.
w: "Can you tell me more about what is worrying you?"
Open-ended questions invite sharing and are professional.
"I'm not sure, but I will find out and let you know."
Honesty with follow-up is professional communication.
"It sounds like you are worried about the procedure."
Reflecting feelings shows listening and is professional.

alt.q: A nervous patient tells a medical assistant she is scared about her biopsy results. Which reply should the assistant AVOID?
alt.ex: Claiming to know exactly how she feels can sound dismissive and is unprofessional.
w: "It sounds like waiting for results is making you anxious."
Reflecting her feelings is a professional response.
"Would you like to tell me what worries you most?"
Inviting her to share is professional communication.
"I can't give results, but I'll ask when they will be ready."
Being honest and following up is professional.

items.q: Leaders should be role models and set a good example. The MOST important trait they should model for their team is _____.
items.ex: Leaders model professionalism so their team sees the expected behavior, attitude, and standards.
w: leadership
Leadership is the role itself; professionalism is the trait leaders should model.
mentoring
Mentoring is guiding a newer worker, not the core trait to model for everyone.
supervision
Supervision is overseeing work, a task rather than a trait to model.

alt.q: Which trait is MOST important for a health care leader to model so the team follows a good example?
alt.ex: Leaders model professionalism so staff see the expected behavior, attitude, and standards.
w: Supervision
Supervision is a task of overseeing work, not a trait to model.
Mentoring
Mentoring guides newer workers; it is not the core trait for everyone.
Strictness
Being strict is not the key trait leaders are expected to model.

alt.q: A nurse manager knows her staff copy how she behaves on the job. Which trait should she MOST importantly display?
alt.ex: Leaders are role models, so professionalism is the most important trait to show.
w: Favoritism toward certain staff
Favoritism damages teamwork and is unprofessional.
Speed over accuracy
Rushing at the expense of accuracy endangers patients.
Criticism without offering solutions
Criticizing without guidance discourages staff and is unprofessional.

items.q: James is working in a busy medical office, and several factors have delayed patient care today. One of the patients is becoming frustrated and loudly complains to James. Which response below is NOT a proper professional response?
items.a: "You shouldn't be so impatient. We have lots of other patients."
items.ex: Blaming the patient for impatience is dismissive; professionals acknowledge frustration and explain the delay.
w: "I'm sorry for the wait. Let me check how much longer it will be."
Apologizing and offering information is a professional response.
"I understand your frustration. Thank you for your patience."
Acknowledging feelings calmly is professional.
"We're running behind today. Would you like to reschedule?"
Explaining the delay and offering options respects the patient.

alt.q: When a frustrated patient loudly complains about delays in a busy office, which staff response is inappropriate?
alt.a: "You shouldn't be so impatient. We have lots of other patients."
alt.ex: Blaming the patient is dismissive; professionals acknowledge frustration and explain delays.
w: "I'm sorry for the wait. Let me check how much longer it will be."
Apologizing and offering information is professional.
"I understand your frustration. Thank you for your patience."
Calmly acknowledging feelings is professional.
"We're running behind today. Would you like to reschedule?"
Explaining the delay and offering options is professional.

alt.q: A pharmacy technician is helping a customer who is upset about a 30-minute wait for a prescription. Which response should the technician AVOID?
alt.a: "You need to calm down; everyone else is waiting too."
alt.ex: Scolding the customer dismisses their frustration instead of addressing it professionally.
w: "I'm sorry about the wait. Let me check on your prescription."
Apologizing and taking action is professional.
"I understand this is frustrating. It should be about ten more minutes."
Acknowledging feelings and giving information is professional.
"We're very busy today. Would you like a call when it's ready?"
Explaining and offering an option respects the customer.

items.q: Lindsay is a new Radiology Technologist in a physician's office. She has a close professional relationship with Alex, a Radiology Technologist who has worked at the office for six years. Alex has excellent professional and technical skills and is always willing to answer Lindsay's questions or give constructive feedback. The term that BEST describes Alex's role is _____.
items.ex: A mentor is an experienced coworker who guides, answers questions, and gives constructive feedback.
w: supervisor
A supervisor has authority to direct and evaluate; Alex is a peer offering guidance.
employer
The employer hires and pays staff; Alex is a fellow technologist.
instructor
An instructor teaches formal classes; Alex informally guides Lindsay on the job.
tf: An experienced coworker who guides a new employee and gives constructive feedback is acting as a mentor.
An experienced coworker who guides a new employee and gives constructive feedback is acting as a supervisor.
A supervisor directs and evaluates work; a peer offering guidance is a mentor.

alt.q: An experienced coworker who willingly answers a new employee's questions and gives constructive feedback is BEST described as a(n) _____.
alt.ex: A mentor is an experienced coworker who guides and gives constructive feedback.
w: supervisor
A supervisor has authority to direct and evaluate, not just guide.
employer
The employer hires and pays staff; it is not a guiding peer.
instructor
An instructor teaches formal classes, not informal on-the-job guidance.

alt.q: During his first months as a pharmacy technician, Carlos is guided by Dana, a technician with ten years' experience who shares tips and gives helpful feedback. Dana is acting as Carlos's _____.
alt.ex: Dana is an experienced peer guiding Carlos with advice and feedback, which is mentoring.
w: supervisor
Dana is a fellow technician, not someone with authority over Carlos.
employer
Dana does not hire or pay Carlos.
patient advocate
A patient advocate speaks for patients, not new coworkers.

items.q: The positive or negative way a person thinks or feels about something or someone is called _____.
items.ex: Attitude is your positive or negative outlook toward people and situations.
w: flexibility
Flexibility is the willingness to adapt to change, not an outlook.
empathy
Empathy is understanding another person's feelings, not your own outlook.
compassion
Compassion is caring about others' suffering, not a positive or negative outlook.
tf: Attitude is the positive or negative way a person thinks or feels about something or someone.
Empathy is the positive or negative way a person thinks or feels about something or someone.
Empathy means understanding another's feelings; attitude is your own positive or negative outlook.

alt.q: A person's positive or negative outlook toward people and situations is known as their _____.
alt.ex: Attitude is your positive or negative way of thinking or feeling about something.
w: flexibility
Flexibility is willingness to adapt to change, not an outlook.
empathy
Empathy is understanding another person's feelings.
compassion
Compassion is caring about others' suffering, not a general outlook.

alt.q: A nursing assistant always expects the worst from her shifts and speaks negatively about every assignment. Which quality does she MOST need to improve?
alt.ex: Her negative way of thinking and feeling about work reflects a poor attitude.
w: Her technical skills
Nothing suggests she lacks skill in performing tasks.
Her punctuality
Nothing in the description involves being late.
Her personal hygiene
Hygiene is unrelated to her negative outlook.

items.q: Karen is trying to choose CEUs for the renewal of her respiratory therapist certification. Which of the following factors should she NOT consider when choosing courses?
items.ex: CEUs should update knowledge and strengthen weak areas, not repeat what she already does well.
w: Areas where her knowledge needs updating
Filling gaps in knowledge is a main purpose of CEUs.
Her certifying body's CEU requirements
Courses must meet the certification's renewal requirements.
New technology and procedures in her field
Keeping current with advances is a key reason for CEUs.
tf: When choosing CEUs, a health care worker should focus on areas needing growth rather than areas of strength.
When choosing CEUs, a health care worker should focus on professional areas they already excel in.
CEUs are meant to strengthen weak areas and update skills, not repeat strengths.
ms: Which factors should Karen consider when choosing CEUs for her respiratory therapist renewal? (Select all that apply)
Requirements of her certifying organization
Courses must count toward her renewal requirements.
Areas where her skills need improvement
CEUs should strengthen weaker areas.
New developments in respiratory care
Staying current with advances is a goal of CEUs.
Professional areas she already excels in
Repeating strengths adds little; focus on growth.
Topics unrelated to her profession
CEUs should relate to her field to count and be useful.

alt.q: Which factor is NOT a good basis for choosing CEU courses to renew a respiratory therapy certification?
alt.a: Professional areas she already excels in
alt.ex: CEUs should update knowledge and strengthen weaker areas, not repeat existing strengths.
w: Areas where her knowledge needs updating
Filling knowledge gaps is a main purpose of CEUs.
Her certifying body's CEU requirements
Courses must meet the certification's renewal rules.
New technology and procedures in her field
Keeping current with advances is a key reason for CEUs.

alt.q: A certified medical assistant is picking CE courses for recertification. Which choice is LEAST useful?
alt.a: A course on a skill she already performs expertly
alt.ex: Repeating strengths adds little; CE should update knowledge or strengthen weak areas.
w: A course on the new EHR software her office just adopted
Learning new technology keeps her current.
A course on a procedure she feels unsure about
Strengthening a weak area is a good use of CE.
A course approved by her certifying organization
Approved courses count toward her renewal requirements.

items.q: Health care professionals are now being cross-trained and becoming multiskilled. The term that describes this trend is _____.
items.ex: Cross-training workers to perform more types of tasks expands their scope of practice.
w: Lifelong learning
Lifelong learning is ongoing education, not the trend of multiskilled roles.
specialization
Specialization narrows a worker's focus, the opposite of multiskilling.
career ladder
A career ladder is levels of advancement, not cross-training across duties.

alt.q: When health care workers learn duties beyond their original training and become multiskilled, this trend is called _____.
alt.ex: Cross-training workers to perform more types of tasks expands their scope of practice.
w: specialization
Specialization narrows focus, the opposite of multiskilling.
career ladder
A career ladder is levels of advancement, not cross-training.
lifelong learning
Lifelong learning is ongoing education, not the multiskilling trend.

alt.q: A small rural clinic trains its medical assistants to also draw blood and perform ECGs. This illustrates which trend?
alt.ex: Cross-training staff to handle more types of tasks expands their scope of practice.
w: Specialization
Specialization narrows duties; these workers are taking on more.
Career ladder
They are not moving up job levels, just adding skills.
Outsourcing
Outsourcing sends work to outside companies, not to cross-trained staff.

items.q: What source should you use to determine the proper dress code for your health care job?
items.ex: Each employer sets its own dress code, so its written policy is the standard to follow.
w: Your coworkers' appearance
Coworkers may not follow policy; the employer's written policy is the standard.
Current uniform fashion trends
Fashion trends do not set workplace requirements.
Your personal style preferences
Personal style must give way to the employer's policy.

alt.q: Where should a health care worker look to learn what clothing and appearance are required on the job?
alt.ex: Each employer sets its own dress code, so its policy is the standard.
w: Your coworkers' appearance
Coworkers may not follow policy correctly.
Current uniform fashion trends
Fashion trends do not set workplace requirements.
Your personal style preferences
Personal style must follow the employer's policy.

alt.q: A new phlebotomist isn't sure whether nail polish and visible tattoos are allowed at her lab. What should she check?
alt.ex: The employer's written policy determines the dress code for that workplace.
w: What other phlebotomists in the lab wear
Coworkers might not be following the policy.
Popular health care uniform websites
Retail websites do not set her employer's rules.
Her own sense of style
Personal preference does not override workplace policy.

items.q: Which of the following situations does NOT illustrate the attention to technical skills required for a professional health care worker?
items.a: Susan has worked in a medical office for one year. She feels that the tasks she performs have become routine, and she takes things for granted.
items.ex: Treating tasks as routine and taking them for granted leads to carelessness and errors.
w: Maria reads professional journals to stay current on new laboratory procedures and equipment.
Keeping knowledge current shows attention to technical skills.
Tom asks his supervisor to review a new procedure with him before performing it on a patient.
Seeking help before an unfamiliar task shows attention to technical skills.
Lena practices a new sterile technique until she can perform it correctly every time.
Practicing until competent shows attention to technical skills.
tf: A worker who sees tasks as routine and takes them for granted is not giving proper attention to technical skills.
Once tasks become routine after a year, a health care worker no longer needs to focus on technical skills.
Technical skills need ongoing attention; complacency with routine tasks causes mistakes.
ms: Which of the following show proper attention to technical skills? (Select all that apply)
Practicing a new procedure until it is performed correctly
Practice builds accurate, safe technique.
Staying current on new equipment and techniques
Technical skills must be updated as practice changes.
Asking for help before performing an unfamiliar procedure
Seeking guidance prevents errors.
Taking routine tasks for granted
Complacency leads to careless mistakes.
Skipping steps when the office is busy
Cutting corners compromises safe, accurate care.

alt.q: Which worker is NOT showing the attention to technical skills expected of a health care professional?
alt.a: A medical office worker of one year who treats her tasks as routine and takes them for granted
alt.ex: Taking tasks for granted leads to carelessness and errors.
w: A lab technician who reads journals to stay current on new procedures
Keeping knowledge current shows attention to technical skills.
A nurse who asks for a review of a new procedure before performing it
Seeking help before an unfamiliar task shows attention to skills.
An assistant who practices a sterile technique until she does it correctly every time
Practicing until competent shows attention to technical skills.

alt.q: A dental assistant has sterilized instruments so many times that she now does it on autopilot without checking her steps. What does this show?
alt.a: A lack of attention to technical skills that can lead to errors
alt.ex: Treating tasks as routine and taking them for granted leads to mistakes.
w: Expert skill that no longer needs careful attention
Even familiar tasks require careful attention to avoid errors.
Efficient time management that should be rewarded
Skipping checks is a safety risk, not good time management.
Proper teamwork with the dentist
Her habit concerns her own skill, not teamwork.

items.q: Jeff knows that CEUs are required every two years for the renewal of his nursing license. To ensure he obtains the required CEUs, Jeff should _____.
items.a: check with his state board of nursing for the specific CEU requirements
items.ex: Each state board of nursing sets its own CEU requirements for license renewal.
w: take any courses offered by his employer
Employer courses may not meet the state's specific requirements.
ask a coworker which courses she took
A coworker's choices may not match current state rules.
rely on his employer to track his CEU hours
Each nurse is responsible for meeting his own license requirements.
tf: To meet license renewal requirements, nurses should check with their state board of nursing for specific CEU rules.
CEU requirements for nursing license renewal are the same in every state.
Each state board of nursing sets its own CEU requirements.

alt.q: A nurse must earn CEUs every two years to renew his license. What is the BEST way to be sure he meets the requirement?
alt.a: Verify the CEU requirements with his state board of nursing
alt.ex: Each state board of nursing sets its own CEU requirements for renewal.
w: Take any courses his employer offers
Employer courses may not meet state requirements.
Ask a coworker which courses she took
A coworker's choices may not match current state rules.
Rely on his employer to track his CEU hours
Each nurse is responsible for meeting his own requirements.

alt.q: A licensed practical nurse moves to a new state and must renew her license there. How should she find out how many CE hours she needs?
alt.a: Contact the new state's board of nursing
alt.ex: CEU requirements are set by each state's board of nursing.
w: Follow her previous state's requirements
Requirements differ from state to state.
Follow a list posted on a nursing blog
Blogs may be outdated or wrong; the board sets the rules.
Assume no CE is needed for her first renewal
She must confirm requirements rather than assume.

items.q: Jane is very active on social media. She is applying for an entry-level job at a local hospital. Which of the following would be MOST likely to affect Jane's chances of being hired if the hiring manager checks Jane's social media?
items.ex: Negative comments about an employer suggest unprofessional behavior and poor judgment to hiring managers.
w: Photos from a family vacation
Ordinary personal photos rarely signal unprofessional behavior.
Posts about her favorite sports team
Harmless hobbies and interests are unlikely to affect hiring.
Pictures of her pets
Pet photos are harmless personal content.
tf: Negative comments about a current employer on social media can hurt an applicant's chances of being hired.
Hiring managers do not look at applicants' public social media when making hiring decisions.
Employers often review public posts, and negative comments suggest unprofessional judgment.
ms: Which social media posts could hurt a health care job applicant's chances of being hired? (Select all that apply)
Complaints about her current employer
Criticizing an employer publicly signals poor professionalism.
Photos showing illegal or unsafe behavior
These raise doubts about judgment and reliability.
Disrespectful comments about coworkers
Publicly criticizing colleagues is unprofessional.
Photos from a family vacation
Ordinary personal photos are not a concern.
Posts about volunteering at a food bank
Community service reflects well on an applicant.

alt.q: If a hospital hiring manager reviews an applicant's social media, which content would MOST likely hurt her chances?
alt.a: Negative comments about her current employer
alt.ex: Criticizing an employer publicly suggests poor judgment and unprofessional behavior.
w: Photos from a family vacation
Ordinary personal photos rarely signal unprofessional behavior.
Posts about her favorite sports team
Harmless interests are unlikely to affect hiring.
Pictures of her pets
Pet photos are harmless personal content.

alt.q: A pharmacy technician applicant posts often online. Which post would MOST concern a hiring manager?
alt.a: "My boss is clueless and this place is a joke."
alt.ex: Publicly criticizing a current employer signals poor judgment to hiring managers.
w: "Great hike with my family this weekend!"
A family outing post is harmless.
"So proud of my daughter's graduation!"
Celebrating family events is harmless.
"Trying a new pasta recipe tonight."
Hobby posts are unlikely to affect hiring.

sections.name: Health Care Systems, Facilities, Insurance, and Current Issues

items.q: Roseanna is discharging to a skilled nursing facility. This is an example of which type of health care facility?
items.ex: A skilled nursing facility provides extended care for people who cannot live independently, so it is long-term care.
w: Hospice facility
Hospice provides comfort care for the dying; Roseanna is recovering from a fracture.
Ambulatory care facility
Ambulatory care is outpatient; patients do not stay overnight.
Hospital facility
Hospitals provide acute care; Roseanna is being discharged from one.

sc.title: Roseanna - discharge planning and Medicare
sc.text: Henry Dodson, a social worker for a hospital, is working on care coordination for Roseanna, a 93-year-old patient discharging to a nursing facility after a hip fracture from a fall at home. Henry notices that Roseanna has Medicare insurance coverage. Roseanna has no living relatives and lives alone in a one-story house. Henry believes that Roseanna will require a long-term stay in the nursing facility and is unsure that Roseanna will ever return to living at the home alone.

alt.q: Henry is arranging Roseanna's move to a skilled nursing facility. Under which category of health care facility does a skilled nursing facility fall?
alt.ex: Skilled nursing facilities provide extended care for those unable to live independently.
w: Hospice facility
Hospice provides comfort care for the dying, not recovery care.
Ambulatory care facility
Ambulatory care is outpatient with no overnight stay.
Hospital facility
Hospitals give acute care; Roseanna is leaving one.

alt.q: A 78-year-old man needs ongoing nursing care after a stroke and is moving into a skilled nursing facility. What type of facility is this?
alt.ex: A skilled nursing facility is a type of long-term care facility.
w: Ambulatory care facility
Ambulatory care is outpatient; he will live at the facility.
Hospice facility
Hospice is for dying patients; he needs ongoing nursing care.
Wellness center
Wellness centers promote fitness and provide no residential care.

items.q: Roseanna explains to Henry that a neighbor fell last month and credited their recovery to the use of acupuncture medicine. Henry knows that acupuncture is a form of complementary, alternative, or integrative medicine known as _____.
items.ex: Acupuncture uses needles at specific points to balance the body's energy flow, an energy theory.
w: homeopathy
Homeopathy uses diluted natural substances that cause symptoms, not energy flow.
massage therapy
Massage manipulates soft tissue; it is a body-based practice.
osteopathy
Osteopathy emphasizes the musculoskeletal system and manipulation, not energy flow.

items.q: Roseanna will be prescribed pain medication at discharge. Limiting the number of pills prescribed
Limiting quantity is a prescribing control, not what the nurse did.
Safe disposal of unused medications
Disposal removes leftover drugs; the nurse is explaining proper use.
