w: Psychosocial conflicts faced across the whole lifespan
Lifespan psychosocial conflicts describe Erikson's stages.
How moral reasoning develops in children and adults
Moral reasoning stages were described by Kohlberg.
A hierarchy of basic human needs
A hierarchy of needs is Maslow's theory.

alt.q: An occupational therapist wants to gauge how a 5-year-old thinks, reasons, and understands the world. Whose stages focus on this kind of development?
alt.ex: Piaget's stages describe the cognitive development of children.
w: Erikson
Erikson's stages describe psychosocial conflicts, not thinking ability.
Kohlberg
Kohlberg's stages describe moral reasoning specifically.
Maslow
Maslow described a hierarchy of needs, not cognitive stages.

items.q: The human rate of development stays fairly constant as individuals move through the lifespan.
items.ex: Development is fastest in infancy and early childhood, then slows and varies through the lifespan.
items.ww: The rate of development changes with age, with rapid spurts early in life and slower change later.

alt.q: Humans develop at roughly the same pace from infancy through old age.
alt.ex: Development is fastest early in life, then slows and varies.
alt.ww: The pace of development changes with age rather than staying steady.

alt.q: The rate of human development varies across the lifespan, with the fastest changes in infancy and early childhood.
alt.ex: Development is fastest early in life, then slows and varies later.
alt.ww: Development does not proceed at a constant rate across life.

items.q: Kohlberg believed that most moral development occurs through law and order.
items.ex: Kohlberg saw moral development progressing through levels of reasoning; law and order is just one stage.
items.ww: Law-and-order thinking is a single stage within Kohlberg's conventional level, not the main source of moral growth.

alt.q: According to Kohlberg, law-and-order thinking is where most moral development takes place.
alt.ex: Kohlberg described moral growth through several levels; law and order is only one stage.
alt.ww: Law and order is a single stage in the conventional level, not the main source of growth.

alt.q: Kohlberg described moral development as moving through several levels of reasoning, with law and order being only one stage.
alt.ex: Kohlberg's theory has multiple levels and stages; law and order is just one.
alt.ww: Kohlberg did not treat law and order as the main source of moral development.

items.q: Which of the following is an example of development?
items.ex: Development is a gain in skills and function; growth is a physical increase in size.
w: Increase in height
Getting taller is a measurable size change, which is growth.
Gain in body weight
Weight gain is a physical size change, so it is growth.
Larger head circumference
Head circumference is a body measurement, which tracks growth.
tf: Gaining social and interpersonal skills is an example of development.
An increase in height is an example of development rather than growth.
Height is a physical size change, which is growth; development refers to skills and function.
ms: Which of the following are examples of development rather than growth? (Select all that apply)
Social and interpersonal skills
Learning to relate to others is a gain in skill, which is development.
Learning to speak in sentences
Language ability is a functional skill, so it is development.
Increase in height
Height is a measurable size change, which is growth.
Gain in body weight
Weight gain is a physical size change, which is growth.

alt.q: Which of the following represents development rather than growth?
alt.ex: Development is a gain in skills and function; growth is a physical size increase.
w: An increase in height
Getting taller is a size change, which is growth.
A gain in body weight
Weight gain is a physical size change, which is growth.
A larger head circumference
Head circumference is a body measurement that tracks growth.

alt.q: During a well-child visit, a nurse records several changes in a 3-year-old. Which one is an example of development?
alt.a: The child now takes turns and plays cooperatively with others
alt.ex: New social skills are a gain in function, which is development.
w: The child grew 3 inches since last year
An increase in height is growth.
The child gained 4 pounds
Weight gain is a size change, which is growth.
The child's shoe size increased
Larger feet reflect a physical size increase, which is growth.

items.q: Which of these pairs of terms is mismatched?
items.ex: Embryogenesis happens in the first trimester (about weeks 1 to 8), so pairing it with the second is wrong.
w: 8th week - all body organs have begun forming
Correct pair: by the 8th week of pregnancy, all body organs have begun forming.
40 weeks - typical full-term pregnancy
Correct pair: about 40 weeks is considered a typical full-term pregnancy.
third trimester - rapid fetal weight gain
Correct pair: the fetus gains most of its weight in the third trimester.
tf: Embryogenesis takes place during the first trimester of pregnancy.
Embryogenesis takes place during the second trimester of pregnancy.
The embryonic period ends around week 8, so embryogenesis is a first-trimester event.

alt.q: Which pairing of a pregnancy time frame with a prenatal event is incorrect?
alt.ex: Embryogenesis occurs in the first trimester, not the second.
w: 8th week - all body organs have begun forming
Correct pair: organ formation has begun by the 8th week.
40 weeks - typical full-term pregnancy
Correct pair: about 40 weeks is a typical full-term pregnancy.
Third trimester - rapid fetal weight gain
Correct pair: the fetus gains most of its weight late in pregnancy.

alt.q: A student makes flashcards on prenatal development. Which card contains an error?
alt.a: Embryogenesis takes place in the second trimester.
alt.ex: Embryogenesis happens in the first trimester, so this card is wrong.
w: All body organs have begun forming by the 8th week.
This card is correct; organ formation has begun by week 8.
A typical full-term pregnancy lasts about 40 weeks.
This card is correct; 40 weeks is typical full term.
The fetus gains most of its weight in the third trimester.
This card is correct; rapid weight gain happens in the third trimester.

items.q: The gradual modification of an organism from conception to maturity is called _____.
items.ex: Development is the gradual change of an organism in function and complexity from conception to maturity.
w: growth
Growth is an increase in physical size, not the whole process of change to maturity.
aging
Aging refers to changes later in life, after maturity is reached.
embryogenesis
Embryogenesis is only the formation of the embryo in the first weeks of pregnancy.
tf: Development is the gradual modification of an organism from conception to maturity.
Growth is the term for the gradual modification of an organism from conception to maturity.
Growth only means an increase in size; the overall process of change is development.

alt.q: What term describes the gradual change an organism undergoes from conception until it reaches maturity?
alt.ex: Development is gradual change in function and complexity from conception to maturity.
w: Growth
Growth is only an increase in physical size.
Aging
Aging refers to changes later in life, after maturity.
Embryogenesis
Embryogenesis is only the formation of the embryo early in pregnancy.

alt.q: An occupational therapist tells parents their child's progress from conception to maturity involves gradual changes in function and complexity, not just size. What is this process called?
alt.ex: Gradual modification from conception to maturity is the definition of development.
w: Growth
Growth refers only to increases in physical size.
Aging
Aging describes changes after maturity, later in life.
Capacitation
Capacitation is a change sperm undergo before fertilization.

items.q: Mammary ducts open to the exterior through a _____.
items.ex: Mammary (lactiferous) ducts carry milk to openings on the nipple, where it exits the body.
w: areola
The areola is the pigmented skin around the nipple; the milk ducts don't open there.
alveolus
Alveoli are the internal sacs that produce milk, not the exterior opening.
lobule
Lobules are internal clusters of milk-producing alveoli deep in the breast.

alt.q: Where do the mammary ducts empty to the outside of the body?
alt.ex: Mammary ducts carry milk to openings on the nipple.
w: At the areola
The areola is the pigmented skin around the nipple, not the duct opening.
At the alveoli
Alveoli are internal milk-producing sacs, not exterior openings.
At the lobules
Lobules are internal clusters of alveoli deep in the breast.

alt.q: A lactation consultant explains how breast milk leaves the body. Through which structure do the mammary ducts open to the exterior?
alt.ex: The mammary ducts end in openings on the nipple, where milk exits.
w: Areola
The areola surrounds the nipple; the ducts do not open there.
Alveoli
Alveoli produce milk inside the breast; they don't open outward.
Lobules
Lobules are internal milk-producing clusters, not exterior openings.

items.q: Which organ provides mechanical protection and nutritional support for the developing embryo?
items.ex: The uterus houses, protects, and nourishes the developing embryo through its lining.
w: ovary
Ovaries produce oocytes and hormones; they don't hold the embryo.
uterine tube
Fertilization usually occurs in the uterine tube, but the embryo implants in the uterus.
cervix
The cervix is the narrow neck of the uterus opening into the vagina, not the embryo's home.

alt.q: Which organ shelters the developing embryo and supplies its nourishment?
alt.ex: The uterus houses, protects, and nourishes the embryo through its lining.
w: Ovary
Ovaries produce oocytes and hormones; they don't hold the embryo.
Uterine tube
Fertilization usually occurs in the uterine tube, but the embryo develops in the uterus.
Cervix
The cervix is the narrow neck of the uterus, not the embryo's home.

alt.q: In a healthy pregnancy, after an embryo implants, which organ gives it physical protection and nutritional support as it develops?
alt.ex: The embryo implants in the uterine lining, which protects and nourishes it.
w: Ovary
Ovaries release oocytes and hormones but do not house the embryo.
Cervix
The cervix opens into the vagina; it is not where the embryo develops.
Vagina
The vagina is the birth canal, not where the embryo grows.

items.q: Sperm cannot fertilize an oocyte until they _____.
items.ex: Capacitation in the female tract changes the sperm membrane so it can penetrate and fertilize the oocyte.
w: undergo cleavage
Cleavage is the cell division of the zygote after fertilization.
shed their flagellum
Sperm need the flagellum to swim to the oocyte.
undergo mitosis
Mature sperm don't divide; they are haploid products of meiosis.

alt.q: Before sperm are able to fertilize an oocyte, what process must they complete?
alt.ex: Capacitation changes the sperm membrane so it can penetrate the oocyte.
w: Cleavage
Cleavage is cell division of the zygote after fertilization.
Loss of the flagellum
Sperm need the flagellum to swim to the oocyte.
Mitosis
Mature sperm don't divide; they are haploid products of meiosis.

alt.q: A fertility specialist explains that freshly released sperm cannot fertilize an egg right away. What change must first occur in the female reproductive tract?
alt.ex: Capacitation in the female tract readies the sperm membrane to fertilize the oocyte.
w: Cleavage of the sperm
Cleavage is division of the zygote, which happens after fertilization.
Implantation of the sperm
Implantation is when the embryo attaches to the uterus after fertilization.
Mitosis of the sperm
Mature sperm do not divide before fertilization.

sections.name: Workplace Safety, Ergonomics, Body Mechanics, and Musculoskeletal Injury Prevention

items.q: Amina explains to the new medical assistants that some ways to help prevent carpal tunnel syndrome include _____.
items.a: using ergonomic keyboards and maintaining wrists in a neutral position while keying
items.ex: Neutral wrists and ergonomic keyboards reduce pressure on the median nerve in the carpal tunnel.
w: resting the wrists on the hard desk edge and bending them upward while keying
Bent wrists and hard edges add pressure on the carpal tunnel, raising risk.
placing the keyboard above elbow height and taking breaks only at lunch
A high keyboard bends the wrists, and infrequent breaks add repetitive strain.
striking keys forcefully and gripping the mouse tightly to keep control
Forceful keying and a tight grip strain wrist tendons and nerves.
tf: Using ergonomic keyboards and keeping wrists neutral while keying helps prevent carpal tunnel syndrome.
Resting the wrists bent upward on the desk edge while keying helps prevent carpal tunnel syndrome.
Bent wrists pressed on a hard edge compress the carpal tunnel, increasing risk.
ms: Which of the following help prevent carpal tunnel syndrome? (Select all that apply)
Using an ergonomic keyboard
Ergonomic keyboards keep the wrists in a more natural position.
Keeping wrists in a neutral position while keying
Neutral wrists reduce pressure on the median nerve.
Taking frequent short breaks to stretch the hands
Breaks interrupt repetitive motion and relieve tendon strain.
Bending the wrists upward while typing
Bent wrists narrow the carpal tunnel and add pressure.
Gripping the mouse tightly
A tight grip increases strain on wrist tendons and nerves.

sc.title: Amina - workstation and injury prevention
sc.text: Amina is an office manager at a busy primary care clinic. This week, there are three medical assistants starting at the clinic, and Amina needs to assist in getting their computer workstations set up. Amina is also responsible for reviewing the policies and procedures regarding proper body mechanics and how to avoid injuries at the workplace.

alt.q: Which practices help reduce the risk of carpal tunnel syndrome?
alt.a: Using an ergonomic keyboard and keeping the wrists neutral while typing
alt.ex: Neutral wrists and ergonomic keyboards reduce pressure on the median nerve.
w: Resting the wrists on the hard desk edge and bending them upward
Bent wrists on hard edges add pressure on the carpal tunnel.
Placing the keyboard above elbow height
A high keyboard bends the wrists and raises risk.
Striking keys forcefully and gripping the mouse tightly
Forceful keying and tight grips strain wrist tendons and nerves.

alt.q: A medical assistant types for hours with her wrists bent upward. What change would best lower her risk of carpal tunnel syndrome?
alt.a: Use an ergonomic keyboard and keep her wrists in a neutral position
alt.ex: Neutral wrist positioning and ergonomic keyboards reduce carpal tunnel pressure.
w: Raise the keyboard above elbow height
A high keyboard bends the wrists further, increasing pressure.
Type more forcefully to finish sooner
Forceful keying strains wrist tendons and nerves.
Grip the mouse more tightly for control
A tight grip adds strain to the wrist.

items.q: Amina is teaching the new medical assistants exercises that can help prevent repetitive motion injuries due to computer use. Amina shows the medical assistants how to slowly rotate the head by tilting it to one side, then rolling to a forward position, and then to the other side. Amina explains the benefit of this exercise is to _____.
items.a: stretch the neck muscles and relieve tension
items.ex: Slow head rolls stretch tight neck muscles and release tension built up from computer work.
w: rest the eyes and reduce eye strain
Eye strain is eased by looking away from the screen, not by head rolls.
strengthen the wrists and prevent carpal tunnel
Head rolls work the neck; wrist exercises target carpal tunnel.
loosen the lower back and prevent lifting injuries
This exercise moves only the head and neck, not the lower back.
tf: Slowly rolling the head from side to side stretches the neck muscles and relieves tension.
Slowly rolling the head from side to side mainly rests the eyes and prevents eye strain.
Eye strain is relieved by eye breaks; head rolls target neck muscle tension.

sc.title: Amina - workstation and injury prevention
sc.text: Amina is an office manager at a busy primary care clinic. This week, there are three medical assistants starting at the clinic, and Amina needs to assist in getting their computer workstations set up. Amina is also responsible for reviewing the policies and procedures regarding proper body mechanics and how to avoid injuries at the workplace.

alt.q: Slowly tilting the head to one side, rolling it forward, then to the other side is an exercise mainly meant to do what?
alt.a: Stretch the neck muscles and relieve tension
alt.ex: Slow head rolls stretch tight neck muscles and release tension from computer work.
w: Rest the eyes and reduce eye strain
Eye strain is eased by looking away from the screen, not head rolls.
Strengthen the wrists and prevent carpal tunnel
Head rolls work the neck, not the wrists.
Loosen the lower back to prevent lifting injuries
This exercise moves only the head and neck.

alt.q: After hours at the front desk computer, a receptionist's neck feels stiff and tight. Which exercise best targets this problem?
alt.a: Slow head rolls: tilt to one side, roll forward, then to the other side
alt.ex: Head rolls stretch the neck muscles and relieve tension.
w: Looking at a distant object for a few seconds
Looking away relieves eye strain, not neck tension.
Wrist flexion and extension stretches
Wrist stretches target the forearm and wrist, not the neck.
Squats with a straight back
Squats work the legs, not the neck muscles.

items.q: Amina explains the importance of early reporting for any injuries or signs and symptoms of injuries. Which of the following could indicate concern for thoracic outlet syndrome?
items.a: Tingling in the neck and shoulders
items.ex: Thoracic outlet syndrome compresses nerves and vessels from the lower neck to the armpit, causing neck and shoulder tingling.
w: Blurred vision and dry, burning eyes
These are signs of computer eye strain, not nerve compression.
Pain on the outside of the elbow when gripping
Outer elbow pain points to tendonitis (tennis elbow), not the thoracic outlet.
Sharp low back pain after lifting a box
Low back pain after lifting suggests an exertion injury.

sc.title: Amina - workstation and injury prevention
sc.text: Amina is an office manager at a busy primary care clinic. This week, there are three medical assistants starting at the clinic, and Amina needs to assist in getting their computer workstations set up. Amina is also responsible for reviewing the policies and procedures regarding proper body mechanics and how to avoid injuries at the workplace.

alt.q: Which symptom might signal thoracic outlet syndrome?
alt.a: Tingling in the neck and shoulders
alt.ex: TOS compresses nerves between the lower neck and armpit, causing neck and shoulder tingling.
w: Blurred vision and dry, burning eyes
These are signs of computer eye strain.
Pain on the outside of the elbow when gripping
Outer elbow pain suggests tendonitis such as tennis elbow.
Sharp low back pain after lifting a box
Low back pain after lifting suggests an exertion injury.

alt.q: A medical assistant reports a pins-and-needles feeling in her neck and shoulders after long computer shifts. Which condition should this raise concern for?
alt.ex: Neck and shoulder tingling can signal compression in the thoracic outlet.
w: Computer eye strain
Eye strain causes blurred vision and dry eyes, not tingling.
Tennis elbow (tendonitis)
Tennis elbow causes outer elbow pain, not neck and shoulder tingling.
A lower back exertion injury
Exertion injuries from lifting cause back pain, not neck tingling.

items.q: Amina is explaining to the medical assistants the importance of preventing exertion injuries, especially when lifting, such as lifting a heavy box of medical equipment in the clinic's supply room. Which of the following is a method of preventing exertion injuries?
items.a: Inhale deeply and tighten your abdominal muscles before lifting.
items.ex: Tightening the abdominal muscles braces and supports the spine during a lift.
w: Bend at the waist and keep your legs straight while lifting.
Bending at the waist loads the back; bend the knees and lift with the legs.
Twist your torso to set the load down beside you.
Twisting while carrying a load is a leading cause of back injury; pivot the feet instead.
Hold the load at arm's length, away from your body.
Loads should be held close to the body to reduce strain on the back.
tf: Inhaling deeply and tightening the abdominal muscles before lifting helps prevent exertion injuries.
Bending at the waist with straight legs before lifting helps prevent exertion injuries.
Bending at the waist strains the back; bend the knees and use the leg muscles.
ms: Which of the following help prevent exertion injuries when lifting? (Select all that apply)
Tightening the abdominal muscles before lifting
Braced abdominal muscles support the spine.
Holding the load close to the body
A close load reduces the strain on the back.
Bending the knees and lifting with the legs
The strong leg muscles take the load instead of the back.
Twisting the torso while carrying the load
Twisting under a load strains the spine; pivot the feet instead.
Bending at the waist with straight legs
This puts the load on the back muscles and spine.

sc.title: Amina - workstation and injury prevention
sc.text: Amina is an office manager at a busy primary care clinic. This week, there are three medical assistants starting at the clinic, and Amina needs to assist in getting their computer workstations set up. Amina is also responsible for reviewing the policies and procedures regarding proper body mechanics and how to avoid injuries at the workplace.

alt.q: Which lifting practice helps prevent exertion injuries?
alt.a: Take a deep breath and tighten the abdominal muscles before lifting
alt.ex: Tightening the abdominal muscles braces and supports the spine during a lift.
w: Bend at the waist and keep the legs straight
Bending at the waist loads the back; bend the knees instead.
Twist the torso to set the load down
Twisting with a load is a leading cause of back injury.
Hold the load at arm's length
Loads should be held close to the body to reduce back strain.

alt.q: A medical assistant is about to lift a heavy box of supplies from the floor. What should she do just before lifting to protect her back?
alt.a: Inhale deeply and tighten her abdominal muscles
alt.ex: Bracing the abdominal muscles supports the spine during the lift.
w: Lock her knees and bend at the waist
Bending at the waist with straight legs strains the back.
Plan to twist her torso to reach the shelf
Twisting while holding a load risks back injury; pivot the feet instead.
Hold the box at arm's length for balance
Holding loads away from the body increases back strain.

items.q: The name for the science of designing and arranging things in working and living environments for maximum efficiency and maximum health and safety is _____.
items.ex: Ergonomics designs and arranges environments to fit people for efficiency, health, and safety.
w: conservative treatment
Conservative treatment is non-surgical care for injuries, not environment design.
exertion
Exertion is physical effort; overexertion causes exertion injuries.
body mechanics
Body mechanics is moving your own body safely, not designing the environment.
tf: Ergonomics is the science of designing and arranging environments for maximum efficiency, health, and safety.
Body mechanics is the science of designing and arranging environments for maximum efficiency, health, and safety.
Body mechanics is how you use your body; designing the environment is ergonomics.

alt.q: Fitting work and living spaces to people so tasks are efficient, healthy, and safe is the focus of which science?
alt.ex: Ergonomics designs and arranges environments for efficiency, health, and safety.
w: Conservative treatment
Conservative treatment is non-surgical injury care, not environment design.
Exertion
Exertion is physical effort, not a design science.
Body mechanics
Body mechanics is moving your own body safely, not designing spaces.

alt.q: A clinic manager adjusts each new employee's chair, monitor height, and keyboard placement to maximize efficiency and prevent injury. What is this an example of?
alt.ex: Arranging the workspace for efficiency, health, and safety is ergonomics.
w: Body mechanics
Body mechanics is how a person moves their own body, not workspace design.
Conservative treatment
Conservative treatment is non-surgical care for injuries that already exist.
Hydrotherapy
Hydrotherapy is water-based treatment, not workspace design.

items.q: A popping, clicking, or cracking sound in the joint is a symptom of a(n) _____.
items.ex: The course lists popping, clicking, or cracking in a joint as a symptom of a repetitive motion injury.
w: fracture
A fracture is a broken bone, marked by deformity, severe pain, and swelling.
sprain
A sprain is a sudden ligament injury from twisting, not ongoing joint noises from overuse.
tear
A tear causes sudden pain and weakness; recurring joint noises point to an RMI.

alt.q: A joint that pops, clicks, or cracks is a symptom of which kind of injury?
alt.ex: The course lists joint popping, clicking, or cracking as an RMI symptom.
w: Fracture
A fracture is a broken bone with deformity, severe pain, and swelling.
Sprain
A sprain is a sudden ligament injury from twisting, not ongoing joint noise.
Tear
A tear causes sudden pain and weakness, not recurring joint noises.

alt.q: A billing clerk notices her wrist clicks and cracks during long days of data entry. According to the course, this symptom points to what?
alt.ex: Joint popping, clicking, or cracking from overuse is an RMI symptom.
w: A fracture
A fracture is a broken bone, marked by deformity and severe pain.
A sprain
A sprain is a sudden twisting injury to a ligament.
A tear
A tear causes sudden pain and weakness, not recurring noises from overuse.

items.q: _____ is/are considered a conservative treatment for repetitive motion injuries (RMIs).
items.ex: Yoga is gentle, non-surgical stretching and strengthening, so it counts as conservative RMI treatment.
w: Antibiotics
Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not overuse injuries.
Surgical release
Surgery is invasive, the opposite of conservative treatment.
Joint replacement
Joint replacement is major surgery, used only when conservative care fails.

alt.q: Which option is a conservative treatment for repetitive motion injuries?
alt.ex: Yoga is gentle, non-surgical stretching and strengthening, so it is conservative.
w: Antibiotics
Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not overuse injuries.
Surgical release
Surgery is invasive, the opposite of conservative treatment.
Joint replacement
Joint replacement is major surgery, used when conservative care fails.

alt.q: A medical assistant with a mild repetitive motion injury wants to avoid invasive care. Which treatment fits a conservative approach?
alt.ex: Yoga is non-invasive stretching and strengthening, a conservative RMI treatment.
w: Surgical tendon release
Tendon release is surgery, so it is not conservative.
Joint replacement surgery
Joint replacement is major surgery, not conservative care.
A course of antibiotics
Antibiotics treat bacterial infections, not overuse injuries.

items.q: The repetitive motion injury that results in compression of the nerves, arteries, or veins in the passageway from the lower neck to the armpit is called _____.
items.ex: The thoracic outlet is the passage from the lower neck to the armpit; compression there is thoracic outlet syndrome.
w: strain
A strain is an overstretched or torn muscle or tendon, not nerve or vessel compression.
tendonitis
Tendonitis is inflammation of a tendon, not compression in the neck-to-armpit passage.
carpal tunnel syndrome
Carpal tunnel compresses the median nerve at the wrist, not near the neck.
tf: Thoracic outlet syndrome involves compression of nerves, arteries, or veins between the lower neck and armpit.
Carpal tunnel syndrome involves compression of nerves, arteries, or veins between the lower neck and armpit.
Carpal tunnel syndrome is median nerve compression at the wrist.

alt.q: Compression of nerves, arteries, or veins in the passage between the lower neck and the armpit is known as what?
alt.ex: The thoracic outlet runs from the lower neck to the armpit; compression there is TOS.
w: Strain
A strain is an overstretched or torn muscle or tendon.
Tendonitis
Tendonitis is inflammation of a tendon, not compression in this passage.
Carpal tunnel syndrome
Carpal tunnel compresses the median nerve at the wrist.

alt.q: A physician tells a patient that repetitive motion has led to nerves and blood vessels being squeezed between the lower neck and armpit. Which diagnosis is this?
alt.ex: Compression in the lower neck-to-armpit passage defines thoracic outlet syndrome.
w: Carpal tunnel syndrome
Carpal tunnel involves median nerve compression at the wrist.
Tendonitis
Tendonitis is tendon inflammation, not nerve and vessel compression.
Sprain
A sprain is a sudden ligament injury, not compression from repetitive motion.

items.q: If an injury is related to job dissatisfaction or when an injury results in the loss of ability to do a favorite activity, _____ might be recommended.
items.ex: Psychotherapy helps when an injury is tied to job dissatisfaction or the emotional loss of a favorite activity.
w: conservative treatment
Conservative treatment addresses physical healing, not the emotional side of an injury.
hydrotherapy
Hydrotherapy uses water to ease pain and stiffness, not emotional issues.
surgery
Surgery repairs tissue damage; it doesn't address dissatisfaction or loss.

alt.q: When an injury is tied to unhappiness at work or keeps a person from a beloved hobby, which type of treatment may be suggested?
alt.ex: Psychotherapy addresses job dissatisfaction and the emotional loss of a favorite activity.
w: Conservative treatment
Conservative treatment targets physical healing, not emotional issues.
Hydrotherapy
Hydrotherapy uses water to ease pain and stiffness, not emotional issues.
Surgery
Surgery repairs tissue; it doesn't address dissatisfaction or loss.

alt.q: A nurse's chronic wrist injury means she can no longer play the piano, her favorite pastime, and she feels down about it. Which treatment may be recommended for this part of her injury?
alt.ex: Losing a favorite activity due to injury is a reason to recommend psychotherapy.
w: Hydrotherapy
Hydrotherapy eases physical pain and stiffness, not emotional loss.
Surgery
Surgery repairs tissue but doesn't address the emotional impact.
Conservative treatment
Conservative treatment focuses on physical healing, not emotional effects.

items.q: Lift teams and the use of specialized equipment are two ways to prevent _____.
items.ex: Lift teams and lifting equipment share or remove heavy loads, preventing overexertion injuries.
w: eye strain
Eye strain is prevented with eye breaks and good screen setup, not lifting help.
repetitive motion injuries
RMIs come from repeated motions and are prevented by breaks and ergonomics.
carpal tunnel syndrome
Carpal tunnel is prevented by neutral wrist positions, not lift teams.
tf: Lift teams and specialized equipment help prevent exertion injuries.
Lift teams and specialized equipment are mainly used to prevent repetitive motion injuries.
Lift teams and equipment reduce heavy-load strain, which prevents exertion injuries.

alt.q: Using lift teams and specialized lifting equipment mainly helps prevent which type of injury?
alt.ex: Lift teams and equipment share or remove heavy loads, preventing overexertion.
w: Eye strain
Eye strain is prevented with eye breaks and good screen setup.
Repetitive motion injuries
RMIs are prevented with breaks and ergonomic changes.
Carpal tunnel syndrome
Carpal tunnel is prevented with neutral wrist positions.

alt.q: A hospital buys mechanical patient lifts and trains staff to move heavy patients in lift teams. Which injury is this mainly intended to prevent?
alt.ex: Lift teams and lifting equipment reduce the load on each worker, preventing exertion injuries.
w: Computer eye strain
Eye strain comes from screen use, not heavy lifting.
Carpal tunnel syndrome
Carpal tunnel comes from wrist positioning during repetitive tasks.
Thoracic outlet syndrome
TOS is a repetitive motion injury, not the target of lift teams.

items.q: To help prevent eye strain when working at the computer, rest the eyes every _____ minutes.
items.ex: Resting the eyes about every 20 minutes (look away at something distant) helps prevent eye strain.
w: The course's recommended interval for eye breaks is every 20 minutes.
Not the course standard; eye breaks are recommended every 20 minutes.
Breaking every 5 minutes isn't the guideline; the course recommends every 20 minutes.
tf: To help prevent eye strain at the computer, rest the eyes every 20 minutes.
To help prevent eye strain at the computer, resting the eyes once every two hours is enough.

The portal of exit is how the pathogen left the original source, such as blood.
tf: In the scenario, the needle serves as the route of transmission in the chain of infection.
In the scenario, the needle serves as the portal of entry in the chain of infection.
The portal of entry is the break in the skin; the needle carries the pathogen.

sc.title: Roseanna - needlestick exposure
sc.text: Roseanna is a new environmental services employee at the local women's health clinic. While emptying a trash can, Roseanna discovers a needle concealed in the side of the bag. As they tie the top of the bag, the needle pricks Roseanna's hand. Roseanna immediately calls Chloe, the clinic receptionist, for assistance.

alt.q: In Roseanna's needlestick, which link in the chain of infection does the needle represent?
alt.ex: The needle carried the pathogen to Roseanna, making it the route of transmission.
w: Infectious agent
The infectious agent is the pathogen itself, not the needle.
Portal of entry
The portal of entry is the break in Roseanna's skin.
Susceptible host
The susceptible host is the person who may become infected, Roseanna.

alt.q: A surgical technician is nicked by a used scalpel contaminated with a patient's blood. In the chain of infection, the scalpel is the:
alt.ex: The scalpel carries the pathogen from the source to the worker, so it is the route.
w: Portal of entry
The portal of entry is the cut in the technician's skin.
Infectious agent
The infectious agent is the pathogen in the blood, not the scalpel.
Portal of exit
The portal of exit is how the pathogen left the patient, such as blood.

items.q: A family member brings flowers to a patient in the hospital but is told that for safety, they are not allowed in the patient's room. This is a type of _____ precaution.
items.ex: Neutropenic precautions protect immunocompromised patients from pathogens carried on flowers, plants, and fresh produce.
w: direct contact
Contact precautions keep a patient's pathogens from spreading to others by touch.
airborne
Airborne precautions stop spread of tiny inhaled particles, using negative-pressure rooms and respirators.
droplet
Droplet precautions guard against large respiratory droplets from coughs and sneezes.
tf: Not allowing flowers in a patient's room is a type of neutropenic precaution.
Not allowing flowers in a patient's room is a type of airborne precaution.
Neutropenic precautions protect patients with weak immunity from pathogens on plants and flowers.

alt.q: Hospital staff ask a visitor to leave a bouquet of flowers outside a patient's room for the patient's safety. Which type of precaution is this?
alt.ex: Neutropenic precautions keep flowers and plants away from patients with weakened immune systems.
w: Contact
Contact precautions keep a patient's pathogens from spreading to others by touch.
Airborne
Airborne precautions use negative-pressure rooms and respirators for inhaled particles.
Droplet
Droplet precautions guard against large respiratory droplets from coughs and sneezes.

alt.q: A patient receiving chemotherapy has a very low white blood cell count and is on neutropenic precautions. Which item should be kept out of the room?
alt.ex: Flowers and plants can carry pathogens that endanger immunocompromised patients.
w: A clean hospital gown
Clean linens are safe and needed for patient care.
Sterile dressing supplies
Sterile supplies are free of pathogens and safe for the patient.
A disinfected stethoscope
Disinfected equipment is safe to use with the patient.

items.q: Spores are thick capsules created by _____ for self-protection.
items.ex: Some bacteria form spores, thick-walled capsules that resist heat and disinfectants until conditions improve.
w: fungi
Fungal spores are mainly for reproduction, not the protective capsules described here.
protozoa
Protozoa are one-celled animal-like organisms; some form cysts, not spores.
viruses
Viruses are not complete cells and do not form spores.
tf: Some bacteria form spores, which are thick capsules created for self-protection.
Viruses form spores, which are thick capsules created for self-protection.
Viruses don't form spores; certain bacteria form protective spores.

alt.q: Which type of microorganism can form spores, thick capsules that protect it?
alt.ex: Some bacteria form thick-walled spores that resist heat and disinfectants.
w: Viruses
Viruses are not complete cells and do not form spores.
Protozoa
Protozoa are one-celled animal-like organisms; some form cysts, not spores.
Rickettsiae
Rickettsiae live inside host cells and do not form protective spores.

alt.q: Tetanus-causing bacteria on a contaminated instrument survive disinfectant by forming thick protective capsules. What are these capsules called?
alt.ex: Bacterial spores are thick capsules that protect bacteria, so sterilization is needed to kill them.
w: Colonies
A colony is a visible group of bacteria growing together, not a protective capsule.
Toxins
Toxins are poisons some bacteria release, not protective coverings.
Antibodies
Antibodies are proteins the human body makes to fight pathogens.

items.q: The general term for a disease that may be transmitted either directly or indirectly from one individual to another is _____.
items.ex: A communicable disease spreads from person to person, directly or indirectly.
w: infectious
Infectious means caused by a pathogen; not every infection spreads between people.
generalized
Generalized describes a disease affecting the whole body, not how it spreads.
viral
Viral describes the cause of a disease, not whether it spreads between people.

alt.q: What general term describes a disease that can pass from one person to another, either directly or indirectly?
alt.ex: A communicable disease spreads from person to person, directly or indirectly.
w: Generalized
Generalized means affecting the whole body, not how a disease spreads.
Chronic
Chronic describes a long-lasting disease, not how it spreads.
Localized
Localized means limited to one area of the body.

alt.q: Chickenpox spreads easily from child to child at a daycare. Which term best describes this kind of disease?
alt.ex: Diseases that pass from person to person are called communicable.
w: Hereditary disease
Hereditary diseases are passed from parent to child through genes.
Localized disease
Localized describes where a disease is in the body, not how it spreads.
Chronic disease
Chronic describes how long a disease lasts, not how it spreads.

items.q: One of the world's most widespread diseases, which is transmitted by mosquitoes, is _____.
items.ex: Malaria is spread by infected mosquitoes and is one of the most widespread diseases in the world.
w: tuberculosis
Tuberculosis spreads through airborne droplets from coughing, not mosquitoes.
acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS)
HIV spreads through blood and body fluids; mosquitoes cannot transmit it.
dysentery
Dysentery spreads through contaminated food or water, not insect bites.
ms: Which of the following diseases are transmitted by mosquitoes? (Select all that apply)
Malaria
Malaria parasites are carried by infected mosquitoes.
West Nile virus
West Nile virus spreads through the bite of infected mosquitoes.
Tuberculosis
TB spreads through airborne droplets from the lungs.
AIDS
HIV spreads through blood and body fluids, not insect bites.
Dysentery
Dysentery spreads through contaminated food or water.

alt.q: Mosquitoes transmit which disease, one of the most widespread in the world?
alt.ex: Malaria is spread by infected mosquitoes and is among the world's most widespread diseases.
w: Tuberculosis
Tuberculosis spreads through airborne droplets, not mosquitoes.
Hepatitis B
Hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids, not insect bites.
Cholera
Cholera spreads through contaminated food or water.

alt.q: A traveler returns from a tropical region with fever and chills after many mosquito bites. Which widespread mosquito-borne disease is a concern?
alt.ex: Malaria is transmitted by mosquitoes and is common in tropical regions.
w: Tuberculosis
Tuberculosis spreads by inhaling infected droplets, not mosquito bites.
AIDS
HIV spreads through blood and body fluids; mosquitoes cannot transmit it.
Dysentery
Dysentery spreads through contaminated food or water.

items.q: The body's natural defense system against infection is called the _____ response.
items.ex: The immune response is the body's natural defense system that recognizes and fights pathogens.
w: aerobic
Aerobic describes organisms that need oxygen to live, not a defense system.
systemic
Systemic means affecting the whole body; it is not the name of the defense system.
anaerobic
Anaerobic describes organisms that live without oxygen.

alt.q: What is the name of the body's natural system for defending against infection?
alt.ex: The immune response recognizes and fights pathogens that invade the body.
w: The systemic response
Systemic means affecting the whole body; it is not the defense system's name.
The aerobic response
Aerobic describes organisms that need oxygen to live.
The anaerobic response
Anaerobic describes organisms that live without oxygen.

alt.q: After receiving a vaccine, a child's body makes antibodies against the pathogen. This is an example of which response?
alt.ex: Making antibodies is part of the body's natural defense, the immune response.
w: Aerobic response
Aerobic refers to needing oxygen, not fighting pathogens.
Anaerobic response
Anaerobic refers to living without oxygen, not body defense.
Opportunistic response
Opportunistic describes infections in weakened bodies, not a defense.

items.q: When an infection occurs due to the weakened physiological state of the body, it is called a(n) _____ infection.
items.ex: Opportunistic infections take advantage of a weakened body, such as in AIDS or cancer treatment.
w: bacterial
Bacterial names the type of pathogen, not the weakened state that allowed infection.
systemic
Systemic means the infection affects the whole body.
severe
Severe describes intensity, not the cause of an infection.
tf: An infection that occurs because the body's defenses are weakened is called an opportunistic infection.
An infection that occurs because the body's defenses are weakened is called a systemic infection.
Systemic means affecting the whole body, not arising from weakened defenses.

alt.q: An infection that takes hold because the body is in a weakened physical state is called a(n) _____ infection.
alt.ex: Opportunistic infections take advantage of a weakened body, such as in AIDS or cancer treatment.
w: localized
Localized means the infection is limited to one area of the body.
systemic
Systemic means the infection affects the whole body.
severe
Severe describes intensity, not why the infection occurred.

alt.q: A patient with advanced AIDS, living at home, develops a fungal infection that rarely affects healthy people. What type of infection is this?
alt.ex: It occurred because AIDS weakened the body, which defines an opportunistic infection.
w: Congenital infection
A congenital infection is present at birth.
Vector-borne infection
Vector-borne infections are spread by insects such as mosquitoes or ticks.
Nosocomial infection
Nosocomial infections are acquired in a health care facility, not at home.

items.q: The general term for removing as many pathogens as possible is _____.
items.ex: Asepsis is the general term for practices that remove or destroy as many pathogens as possible.
w: defense method
This is not a recognized infection control term.
bacteriostatic
Bacteriostatic agents only stop bacterial growth; they don't remove pathogens.
antiseptic technique
Antiseptics inhibit growth on skin; it is one method, not the general term.

alt.q: What is the general term for practices that remove or destroy as many pathogens as possible?
alt.ex: Asepsis is the general term for removing or destroying as many pathogens as possible.
w: Contamination
Contamination means pathogens are present, the opposite of asepsis.
Bacteriostasis
Bacteriostasis only stops bacterial growth; it does not remove pathogens.
Inflammation
Inflammation is a body defense reaction, not a pathogen-removal practice.

alt.q: Before a procedure, a medical assistant cleans the work area and their hands to get rid of as many pathogens as possible. This overall goal is known as:
alt.ex: Asepsis is the effort to remove or destroy as many pathogens as possible.
w: Contamination
Contamination is the presence of pathogens, not their removal.
Infection
Infection is pathogens invading and multiplying in the body.
Immunity
Immunity is the body's resistance to disease, not a cleaning practice.

items.q: In U.S. hospitals, the number of annual deaths from nosocomial infections is approximately _____.
items.ex: Nosocomial (health care-associated) infections cause roughly 100,000 deaths a year in U.S. hospitals.
w: This underestimates the yearly death toll from nosocomial infections.
This overestimates the commonly cited figure of about 100,000.
This is double the commonly cited figure of about 100,000.
tf: Nosocomial infections cause approximately 100,000 deaths per year in U.S. hospitals.
Nosocomial infections cause approximately 10,000 deaths per year in U.S. hospitals.
The commonly cited figure is about 100,000 deaths per year.

alt.q: Approximately how many people die each year from nosocomial infections in U.S. hospitals?
alt.ex: The commonly cited figure is about 100,000 deaths a year from nosocomial infections.
w: About 10,000
This greatly underestimates the yearly death toll.
About 50,000
This is half the commonly cited figure of about 100,000.
About 250,000
This overestimates the commonly cited figure of about 100,000.

alt.q: An infection control nurse tells new staff that infections acquired in U.S. hospitals cause roughly how many deaths each year?
alt.ex: Health care-associated infections cause roughly 100,000 deaths a year in U.S. hospitals.
w: About 1,000
This vastly underestimates the yearly death toll.
About 25,000
This is far below the commonly cited figure of about 100,000.
About 500,000
This is far above the commonly cited figure of about 100,000.

items.q: One of the reasons that hepatitis B is highly contagious is that the virus _____.
items.a: can remain active for several days in dried blood
items.ex: HBV survives on surfaces in dried blood for days, so contaminated items can spread it long after exposure.
w: is spread through casual contact such as hugging
Hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids, not casual contact.
can survive for only a few minutes outside the body
The opposite is true; its long survival makes it highly contagious.
is transmitted mainly through the bites of mosquitoes
Mosquitoes do not transmit hepatitis B; blood and body fluids do.

alt.q: Which feature of the hepatitis B virus helps make it highly contagious?
alt.a: It can remain active for several days in dried blood
alt.ex: Surviving for days in dried blood lets contaminated items spread HBV long after exposure.
w: It spreads through casual contact such as hugging
Hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids, not casual contact.
It dies within a few minutes outside the body
The opposite is true; its long survival makes it highly contagious.
It is spread mainly by mosquito bites
Mosquitoes do not transmit hepatitis B.

alt.q: A housekeeper finds a dried blood spot on a bed rail in a hepatitis B patient's room. Why must it be treated as infectious?
alt.a: Hepatitis B can remain active in dried blood for several days
alt.ex: HBV survives for days in dried blood, so old spills can still transmit it.
w: Dried blood is only infectious if it is still warm
Temperature does not matter; HBV survives in dried blood for days.
Hepatitis B spreads mainly through the air from dried blood
Hepatitis B spreads through blood and body fluids, not the air.
Hepatitis B can be caught by simply entering the room
Casual presence in a room does not spread hepatitis B.

items.q: How are the forms of typhus caused by rickettsia transmitted from person to person?
items.ex: Rickettsiae live in lice, fleas, ticks, and mites, which transmit typhus through their bites.
w: Fecal material
Fecal-oral spread causes diseases like dysentery, not typhus.
Coughing and sneezing
Respiratory droplets spread diseases like influenza, not rickettsial typhus.
Touching an infected person
Typhus requires an insect vector; touching an infected person does not spread it.

alt.q: Typhus caused by rickettsiae spreads from person to person by what means?
alt.a: Bites of certain insects, such as lice, fleas, and ticks
alt.ex: Rickettsiae live in insects, which transmit typhus through their bites.
w: Contact with fecal material
Fecal-oral spread causes diseases like dysentery, not typhus.
Respiratory droplets from coughing
Respiratory droplets spread diseases like influenza, not rickettsial typhus.
Touching an infected person's skin
Typhus needs an insect vector; touching an infected person does not spread it.

alt.q: During a typhus outbreak in a crowded shelter, which control measure targets how rickettsial typhus spreads?
alt.ex: Typhus is spread by insect bites, so removing lice and fleas breaks transmission.
w: Boiling all drinking water
Boiling water prevents waterborne illness, not insect-borne typhus.
Having everyone wear surgical masks
Masks block respiratory droplets, which do not spread typhus.
Avoiding handshakes
Typhus is not spread by touching people; insects carry it.

items.q: A urine sample has splashed onto the countertop. Which method of cleaning would be appropriate?
items.ex: Disinfectants are chemicals used on surfaces to destroy pathogens, suitable for body fluid spills on counters.
w: Antiseptic
Antiseptics are used on skin and living tissue, not countertops.
Sterilization
Sterilization by autoclave is for instruments, not fixed surfaces like countertops.
Plain water and paper towels
Water alone does not destroy pathogens in body fluids.
tf: A urine spill on a countertop should be cleaned with a disinfectant.
A urine spill on a countertop should be cleaned with an antiseptic.
Antiseptics are for skin and living tissue; disinfectants are for surfaces.

alt.q: Urine has splashed onto a lab countertop. What is the appropriate way to clean the surface?
alt.ex: Disinfectants are chemicals that destroy pathogens on surfaces like countertops.
w: Use an antiseptic
Antiseptics are used on skin and living tissue, not countertops.
Sterilize it in an autoclave
Autoclaves sterilize instruments, not fixed surfaces like counters.
Wipe it with plain water
Water alone does not destroy pathogens in body fluids.

alt.q: A patient's blood drips onto an exam room counter during a draw. Which product should the medical assistant use to clean the counter?
alt.ex: Disinfectants destroy pathogens on nonliving surfaces after body fluid spills.
w: An antiseptic skin cleanser
Antiseptics are meant for skin, not countertops.
Autoclave sterilization
Counters cannot go in an autoclave; it is for instruments.
Dry paper towels only
Wiping alone does not destroy pathogens left behind.

items.q: A major purpose of transmission precautions is to prevent epidemics.
items.ex: Transmission-based precautions stop pathogens from spreading through a facility and community, preventing epidemics.
items.ww: Isolating infectious patients is a key way to keep a single case from becoming an outbreak.

alt.q: Preventing epidemics is one of the main purposes of transmission-based precautions.
alt.ex: Precautions stop pathogens from spreading through a facility and community.
alt.ww: Isolating infectious patients keeps single cases from becoming outbreaks, so this is not false.

alt.q: Transmission precautions protect only the individual patient and play no role in preventing epidemics.
alt.ex: A key purpose of transmission precautions is stopping spread that could cause epidemics.
alt.ww: Preventing wider spread is a main goal, so this statement cannot be true.

items.q: Proper handwashing is an effective way to break the chain of infection.
items.ex: Handwashing breaks the chain at the mode of transmission by removing pathogens from hands.
items.ww: Hands are a main route of spread, so proper handwashing does break the chain of infection.

alt.q: Washing hands correctly is an effective way to interrupt the chain of infection.
alt.ex: Handwashing removes pathogens from hands, breaking the chain at the mode of transmission.
alt.ww: Hands are a main route of spread, so this statement is not false.

alt.q: Handwashing removes dirt but cannot break the chain of infection.
alt.ex: Proper handwashing removes pathogens and breaks the chain of infection.
alt.ww: Handwashing does interrupt transmission, so this statement cannot be true.

items.q: Bacteria are round, two-celled organisms.
items.ex: Bacteria are one-celled organisms with several shapes: round (cocci), rod (bacilli), and spiral (spirilla).
items.ww: Bacteria are single-celled, not two-celled, and are not only round.

alt.q: Bacteria are two-celled organisms that are always round.
alt.ex: Bacteria are one-celled and can be round, rod-shaped, or spiral.
alt.ww: Bacteria are neither two-celled nor only round, so this is not true.

alt.q: Bacteria are one-celled organisms that can be round, rod-shaped, or spiral.
alt.ex: Bacteria are single-celled and occur as cocci, bacilli, and spirilla.
alt.ww: This correctly describes bacteria, so calling it false would be wrong.

items.q: Following standard precautions with all patients helps prevent the health care professional from becoming infected with hepatitis B or HIV.
items.ex: Standard precautions treat all blood and body fluids as infectious, protecting workers from bloodborne pathogens.
items.ww: Standard precautions are designed specifically to prevent bloodborne infections like hepatitis B and HIV.

alt.q: Using standard precautions with every patient helps protect health care workers from hepatitis B and HIV.
alt.ex: Standard precautions treat all blood and body fluids as infectious, blocking bloodborne pathogens.
alt.ww: Standard precautions are designed to prevent bloodborne infections, so this is not false.

alt.q: Standard precautions only need to be used with patients known to have hepatitis B or HIV.
alt.ex: Standard precautions apply to all patients because infection status is often unknown.
alt.ww: Limiting precautions to known cases would leave workers exposed to undiagnosed infections.

items.q: Sterile gloves should be worn when coming in contact with blood or other body fluids while caring for patients.
items.ex: Clean nonsterile gloves are used for contact with blood or body fluids; sterile gloves are for sterile procedures.
items.ww: Standard precautions call for clean gloves, not sterile ones, for routine contact with body fluids.

alt.q: Health care workers must wear sterile gloves whenever they touch blood or body fluids during patient care.
alt.ex: Clean nonsterile gloves are used for body fluid contact; sterile gloves are for sterile procedures.
alt.ww: Standard precautions call for clean gloves, not sterile ones, so this is not true.

alt.q: Clean, nonsterile gloves are appropriate for routine contact with a patient's blood or body fluids.
alt.ex: Standard precautions call for clean gloves for body fluid contact.
alt.ww: Sterile gloves are reserved for sterile procedures, so this statement is not false.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the body's defense mechanisms against infection?
items.ex: High blood pressure is a health problem, not a defense; the body defends with barriers, fever, and reflexes.
w: Mucus in the nose
True defense: mucus traps pathogens before they enter the respiratory tract.
Fever
True defense: a raised temperature slows pathogen growth and boosts immune activity.
Coughing
True defense: coughing expels pathogens and irritants from the airway.
ms: Which of the following are body defense mechanisms against infection? (Select all that apply)
Mucus in the nose
Mucus traps pathogens before they enter the airway.
Coughing
Coughing forces pathogens out of the respiratory tract.
Fever
Fever slows pathogen growth and boosts immune activity.
High blood pressure
High blood pressure is a health problem, not a defense.
Low blood sugar
Low blood sugar weakens the body and does not fight pathogens.

alt.q: Which of these does NOT help the body defend itself against infection?
alt.ex: High blood pressure is a health problem, not one of the body's infection defenses.
w: Tears
True defense: tears wash pathogens away from the eyes.
Stomach acid
True defense: acid in the stomach destroys swallowed pathogens.
Coughing
True defense: coughing expels pathogens and irritants from the airway.

alt.q: A patient asks which body processes protect against germs. Which item should the medical assistant NOT include?
alt.ex: High blood pressure does not protect against pathogens; it is a health problem.
w: Fever
True defense: a raised temperature slows pathogen growth.
Sneezing
True defense: sneezing expels pathogens from the nose.
Mucus in the nose
True defense: mucus traps pathogens before they enter the airway.

items.q: Different bacterial infections respond to different antibiotics.
items.ex: Each antibiotic works against certain bacteria, so the right drug depends on the specific infection.
items.ww: No single antibiotic kills all bacteria, which is why cultures guide antibiotic choice.

alt.q: Not every bacterial infection responds to the same antibiotic; each responds to particular drugs.
alt.ex: Each antibiotic works against certain bacteria, so the drug must match the infection.
alt.ww: No single antibiotic kills all bacteria, so this statement is not false.

alt.q: A single antibiotic works equally well against every type of bacterial infection.
alt.ex: Different bacteria respond to different antibiotics, so cultures guide drug choice.
alt.ww: No antibiotic works against all bacteria, so this statement cannot be true.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT a reason that some bacteria have become drug-resistant?
items.a: Decreased research into developing new antibiotics
items.ex: Resistance comes from how antibiotics are used; less research limits new drugs but does not cause resistance.
w: Overuse of antibiotics
True reason: frequent antibiotic use lets resistant bacteria survive and multiply.
Patients not taking the full course of antibiotics
True reason: stopping early leaves the strongest bacteria alive to multiply.
Use of antibiotics in animal feed
True reason: antibiotics in livestock expose bacteria to drugs, promoting resistance.
ms: Which of the following are reasons some bacteria have become drug-resistant? (Select all that apply)
Overuse of antibiotics
Frequent use lets resistant bacteria survive and multiply.
Patients not finishing their full course of antibiotics
Stopping early leaves the hardiest bacteria alive.
Use of antibiotics in animal feed
Exposing bacteria in livestock to antibiotics promotes resistance.
Decreased research into developing new antibiotics
This limits new treatments but does not cause bacteria to become resistant.
Frequent handwashing by health care workers
Handwashing reduces spread of all bacteria, including resistant ones.

alt.q: All of the following have contributed to drug-resistant bacteria EXCEPT:
alt.a: Decreased research into developing new antibiotics
alt.ex: Resistance comes from how antibiotics are used; less research limits new drugs but doesn't cause resistance.
w: Overuse of antibiotics
True reason: frequent use lets resistant bacteria survive and multiply.
Patients not finishing their full course of antibiotics
True reason: stopping early leaves the strongest bacteria alive.
Use of antibiotics in animal feed

alt.q: An infection control nurse lists causes of antibiotic resistance for new staff. Which item does NOT belong on the list?
alt.a: Decreased research into developing new antibiotics
alt.ex: Less research slows new drug development but is not what makes bacteria resistant.
w: Prescribing antibiotics for viral illnesses like colds
True reason: unnecessary use exposes bacteria to drugs and promotes resistance.

items.q: Viruses are incomplete cells and depend on other cells for nutrition.
items.ex: Viruses are not complete cells; they must live inside other living cells to grow and reproduce.
items.ww: Viruses cannot survive or reproduce on their own; they depend on host cells.

alt.q: Because viruses are not complete cells, they rely on other living cells for nutrition.
alt.ex: Viruses must live inside host cells to get nutrition and reproduce.
alt.ww: Viruses cannot survive or reproduce on their own, so this is not false.

alt.q: Viruses are complete cells that can grow and reproduce on their own without a host.
alt.ex: Viruses are incomplete cells that depend on host cells to live and reproduce.
alt.ww: Viruses cannot reproduce without host cells, so this statement cannot be true.

items.q: HIV can be transmitted by shaking hands with someone who is infected with the virus.
items.ex: HIV spreads through blood and certain body fluids, not casual contact like handshakes.
items.ww: Intact skin contact such as a handshake does not transmit HIV.

alt.q: Shaking hands with a person who has HIV can spread the virus.
alt.ex: HIV spreads through blood and certain body fluids, not casual contact.
alt.ww: Intact skin contact like a handshake does not transmit HIV, so this is not true.

alt.q: HIV is spread through blood and certain body fluids, not by casual contact such as a handshake.
alt.ex: HIV requires contact with infected blood or body fluids to spread.
alt.ww: Casual contact does not transmit HIV, so this statement is not false.

items.q: All molds are pathogenic.

items.ww: Some molds are nonpathogenic and even beneficial, like the mold used to make penicillin.

alt.q: Every type of mold causes disease.

alt.q: Some molds are harmless or even helpful, such as the mold used to make penicillin.
alt.ex: Only some molds are pathogenic; others are harmless or beneficial.
alt.ww: Not all molds cause disease, so this statement is not false.

items.q: It is only necessary to wash your hands before putting on gloves.

items.ww: Gloves can tear or be contaminated on removal, so hands are also washed after gloves come off.

alt.q: Hands need to be washed before putting on gloves, but not after taking them off.
alt.ex: Hands must be washed both before putting on gloves and after removing them.
alt.ww: Gloves can leak or contaminate hands on removal, so washing after is required.

alt.q: Hands should be washed both before putting on gloves and after removing them.

items.q: Where must sterile objects be located in relation to the health care professional?

Behind the professional's back

Behind the professional's back

At knee level

items.q: Most major health care regulations and investigations occur at the local level.
items.ex: Major health care regulations and investigations happen at the federal and state levels, through agencies like CDC and OSHA.
items.ww: Federal agencies such as CDC, FDA, and OSHA, along with state agencies, handle most major regulation.

alt.q: The local level is where most major health care regulations and investigations take place.
alt.ex: Major regulations and investigations happen at the federal and state levels.
alt.ww: Agencies such as CDC, FDA, and OSHA work at the federal level, so this is not true.

alt.q: Most major health care regulations and investigations occur at the federal and state levels.
alt.ex: Federal agencies like CDC and OSHA, plus state agencies, handle most major regulation.
alt.ww: Major regulation is not mainly local, so this statement is not false.

sections.name: Safety, Emergency Preparedness, Workplace Hazards, and Disaster Response

items.q: What should Alita have done if a safe evacuation was not possible?
items.a: Attempted to extinguish the fire using a fire extinguisher
items.ex: If evacuation isn't possible, the course says to fight a small fire with an extinguisher using PASS.
w: Used the elevator to leave the building as quickly as possible
Elevators must never be used during a fire; they can fail or open onto fire floors.
Opened the windows to let the smoke out of the office
Opening windows feeds the fire oxygen and spreads smoke.
Hidden under a desk until firefighters arrived
Hiding makes rescue harder and does nothing to control the fire.

sc.title: Alita - fire and evacuation
sc.text: Alita works as a medical records clerk in a hospital, managing patient records, updating databases, and ensuring the accuracy and confidentiality of medical information. One day, Alita notices the strong odor of smoke coming from the hallway outside of the office door. Alita checks the hospital's emergency response procedures, activates the fire alarm, informs colleagues about the potential fire, and directs them to evacuate safely. Once outside, Alita takes charge of the department's evacuation procedures, ensures everyone is accounted for, assists those who need extra support, and brings the department's emergency preparedness plan.

alt.q: If Alita had been unable to evacuate safely, what would the correct action have been?
alt.a: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher
alt.ex: When evacuation isn't possible, the course says to fight the fire with an extinguisher using PASS.
w: Take the elevator to leave quickly
Elevators must never be used during a fire.
Open the windows to let out the smoke
Opening windows feeds the fire oxygen and spreads smoke.
Hide under a desk until firefighters arrive
Hiding makes rescue harder and does nothing to control the fire.

alt.q: A nurse finds a small trash can fire, and smoke is blocking the only exit hallway. What should the nurse do?
alt.a: Use a fire extinguisher on the fire with the PASS method
alt.ex: If safe evacuation is not possible, the next step is to fight the fire with an extinguisher.
w: Use the elevator to escape the floor
Elevators can fail or open onto fire floors during a fire.
Open the windows to vent the smoke
Fresh air feeds the fire and spreads smoke.
Prop the door open so others can see the fire
An open door lets fire and smoke spread to other areas.

items.q: What is the purpose of an emergency preparedness plan?
items.a: To outline procedures for responding to various emergencies
items.ex: An emergency preparedness plan spells out who does what, who reports, and how to communicate in a disaster.
w: To document who caused an emergency after it occurs
Fault-finding is not its purpose; incident reports document events afterward.
To replace the need for regular fire and disaster drills
Drills are part of preparedness; the plan doesn't replace them.
To track employee attendance during normal operations
Attendance tracking is routine management, not emergency planning.

sc.title: Alita - fire and evacuation
sc.text: Alita works as a medical records clerk in a hospital, managing patient records, updating databases, and ensuring the accuracy and confidentiality of medical information. One day, Alita notices the strong odor of smoke coming from the hallway outside of the office door. Alita checks the hospital's emergency response procedures, activates the fire alarm, informs colleagues about the potential fire, and directs them to evacuate safely. Once outside, Alita takes charge of the department's evacuation procedures, ensures everyone is accounted for, assists those who need extra support, and brings the department's emergency preparedness plan.

alt.q: Why does a health care facility have an emergency preparedness plan?
alt.a: To outline how to respond to different kinds of emergencies
alt.ex: The plan spells out who reports, each person's duties, and how to communicate in a disaster.
w: To determine who is to blame after an emergency
Fault-finding is not its purpose; incident reports document events afterward.
To replace the need for fire and disaster drills
Drills are part of preparedness; the plan does not replace them.
To track employee attendance during normal operations
Attendance tracking is routine management, not emergency planning.

alt.q: During a tornado warning, hospital staff check a document listing who reports to work, each person's duties, and how to communicate. What is this document?
alt.ex: An emergency preparedness plan outlines procedures for responding to emergencies.
w: An incident report
An incident report documents an accident or error after it happens.
A safety data sheet
A safety data sheet gives information about a specific chemical.
The patient's medical record
The medical record documents a patient's care, not disaster procedures.

items.q: Alita was able to accurately detect a potential fire in the office. A fire is considered which type of workplace hazard?
items.ex: Physical hazards, like fire, can cause physical injury and tissue damage such as burns.
w: environmental
Not the course's category for fire; fire causes tissue damage, which makes it a physical hazard.
ergonomic
Ergonomic hazards come from body position and repetitive motion, like poor workstation setup.
psychosocial
Psychosocial hazards involve stress, emotional strain, and lack of support.
ms: Which of the following are examples of physical hazards in the workplace? (Select all that apply)
Fire
Fire can cause burns and tissue damage, so it is a physical hazard.
Frayed electrical cords that can cause shock
Electrical shock causes physical injury, a physical hazard.
Constant emotional demands without supervisory support
This is a psychosocial hazard.
Poorly positioned keyboard used all day
This is an ergonomic hazard that leads to repetitive motion injury.

sc.title: Alita - fire and evacuation
sc.text: Alita works as a medical records clerk in a hospital, managing patient records, updating databases, and ensuring the accuracy and confidentiality of medical information. One day, Alita notices the strong odor of smoke coming from the hallway outside of the office door. Alita checks the hospital's emergency response procedures, activates the fire alarm, informs colleagues about the potential fire, and directs them to evacuate safely. Once outside, Alita takes charge of the department's evacuation procedures, ensures everyone is accounted for, assists those who need extra support, and brings the department's emergency preparedness plan.

alt.q: What category of workplace hazard does a fire fall into?
alt.ex: Fire can cause physical injury and tissue damage such as burns, making it a physical hazard.
w: Ergonomic
Ergonomic hazards come from body position and repetitive motion.
Psychosocial
Psychosocial hazards involve stress, emotional strain, and lack of support.
Biological
Biological hazards involve pathogens such as bacteria and viruses.

alt.q: Flames from an electrical fire in a records office burn a staff member's hand. This injury came from which type of workplace hazard?
alt.ex: Physical hazards, like fire, cause physical injury and tissue damage.
w: Ergonomic
Ergonomic hazards involve poor posture and workstation setup.
Psychosocial
Psychosocial hazards involve stress and emotional strain, not burns.
Biological
Biological hazards involve infectious agents, not flames.

items.q: Based on the example in the text, what is the correct emergency code for a fire or smoke?
items.ex: Code red is the standard code for fire or smoke; using codes alerts staff without alarming patients.
w: Code blue
Code blue commonly signals cardiac or respiratory arrest.
Code pink
Code pink commonly signals an infant or child abduction.
Code silver
Code silver commonly signals a person with a weapon or an active shooter.
tf: In the textbook example, Code red is the emergency code for a fire or smoke.
In the textbook example, Code blue is the emergency code for a fire or smoke.
Code blue commonly signals cardiac or respiratory arrest; Code red signals fire.

sc.title: Alita - fire and evacuation
sc.text: Alita works as a medical records clerk in a hospital, managing patient records, updating databases, and ensuring the accuracy and confidentiality of medical information. One day, Alita notices the strong odor of smoke coming from the hallway outside of the office door. Alita checks the hospital's emergency response procedures, activates the fire alarm, informs colleagues about the potential fire, and directs them to evacuate safely. alt.q: In the text's example, which emergency code signals fire or smoke?
alt.ex: Code red is the code for fire or smoke, alerting staff without alarming patients.
w: Code blue
Code blue commonly signals cardiac or respiratory arrest.
Code pink
Code pink commonly signals an infant or child abduction.
Code silver
